CALL DATE: 2026-02-17
ATTENDEES: Sawan Kapoor (sawankapoor@hotmail.com), Manish (Success Gyan team)
COMPANY: Success Gyan
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
Sawan Kapoor runs the career coaching vertical within Success Gyan, the largest webinar and seminar company in India with 10 verticals and ~150,000 new clients per vertical per year. They have been on Teachable for 5-6 years and were flagged due to exceeding the Growth plan's 5,000-user limit. Sawan was quoted a ~$12,000/yr increase (~600% over current $190/mo) and is pushing back hard, citing a prior Teachable support screenshot promising unlimited students on Growth. He wants to stay but will migrate if forced into a large increase.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Host career coaching courses for students who convert through webinar funnels
Audience: Indian professionals seeking career advancement, coaching certifications
Business model: Paid courses (payment collected via Razorpay locally, enrollment via Zapier integration)
Content types: Video courses across multiple verticals (career coaching, life coaching, neuroscience, spiritual healing, personal branding)
Scale expectations: 25 courses at Growth plan cap, 10 verticals with 150K new clients/year each, planning a second school for personal leadership

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Currently paying ~$190/mo (~$2,280/yr). Previous plan was ~$1,000/yr before price increase. Cannot absorb 600% increase — India is price-sensitive market, cannot pass costs to customers.
Authority: Sawan runs career coaching vertical but cannot make decisions for other verticals (e.g., switching to Teachable Pay requires buy-in from other vertical heads).
Need: Course hosting, reliable video streaming, unlimited (or high-cap) student enrollment, international payment support.
Timeline: Immediate — team already started looking at alternatives after receiving the price increase email.

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Zapier (enrollment automation from local payment gateway to Teachable), Razorpay (Indian payment gateway)
Reporting needs: Not discussed
Payments / checkout: Local Indian payment gateway (Razorpay) due to RBI regulations on international money movement; W2 complications with direct Teachable payments; declined Teachable Pay switch due to complexity and multi-vertical governance
Admin or seat management: Multi-vertical ecosystem, each vertical has its own head; Sawan cannot mandate changes across verticals
Special workflows or constraints: Indian regulatory environment (Reserve Bank of India), international payout compliance issues

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- 5-6 year loyal customer, absorbed prior 2x price increase without complaint
- Actively recommends Teachable to coached coaches (estimated 1,000+ coaches on Teachable because of Success Gyan)
- Planning to launch a second school (personal leadership) in Q1-Q2 of Indian FY (April-Sept 2026)
- Expressed desire to stay: "we want to stay with Teachable... it's a beautiful symbiotic relationship"

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- 600% price increase is a dealbreaker — "I'd be in losses"
- Team already started evaluating alternatives
- Teachable support told them unlimited students on Growth — has screenshot evidence
- Cannot switch to Teachable Pay due to Indian payment regulations and multi-vertical governance
- Video buffering issues at 55-60 min mark degrading student experience
- Customer support quality insufficient — sends articles instead of hands-on help
- If they leave, all downstream Teachable referrals from 10 verticals stop (organic growth channel lost)

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Videos buffering at 55 min to 1 hour mark
- Customer support sends articles instead of providing direct help
- Growth plan 25-course limit is at capacity
- International payout process is too complicated (W2 requirement)

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Currently on Growth (~$190/mo). Previously on highest plan (~$1,000/yr before increase). Kevin suggested ~$7,000/yr — rejected.
Discounts offered: Kevin exploring options, mentioned Teachable Pay switch could avoid increase.
Contract length discussed: Currently annual billing.
Constraints or approvals needed: Multi-vertical governance — Sawan cannot mandate Teachable Pay switch for all verticals.

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Take screenshots (from Sawan showing unlimited students promise) back to team
- Come back with a retention offer today
- Explore what pricing team can work out given the support screenshot error

Customer:
- Send screenshots of Teachable support confirming unlimited students on Growth
- Continue evaluating alternatives in parallel

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Sawan is articulate, firm but polite. He clearly framed the conversation as a retention issue rather than a negotiation — emphasizing the downstream referral value Success Gyan brings. He was strategic in mentioning the volume of coaches they've driven to Teachable and the organic growth that would cease. Manish (team member) was mostly silent. The call had a warm, professional tone. Kevin was empathetic but limited in what he could offer on the spot.

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-02-17
ATTENDEES: jozephdanial@gmail.com
COMPANY: Jozeph Danial
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
Jozeph Ezzat Danial is an Egyptian course creator with ~800k social media followers across Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok. He sells low-ticket courses (~$5 each) to a young Egyptian audience, collecting payments via E-wallets (mobile electronic wallets) outside of Teachable Pay. He is on the Growth plan and was surprised by the $12,000/year price increase related to exceeding the 5,000 student limit. Kevin proposed a custom plan at ~$7,000 with unlimited students.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Sell affordable educational courses to young Arabic-speaking audience
Audience: Young Egyptians and MENA region learners, mostly without credit cards
Business model: High-volume, low-ticket ($5/course) with manual E-wallet payment collection
Content types: Courses with assignments, certificates, gamification
Scale expectations: Already exceeding 5,000 students, growing via 800k social following

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Current plan cost is a concern; $12K/year too high, competitor offers pay-per-student at $0.75
Authority: Jozeph is the sole decision-maker
Need: Needs unlimited students, E-wallet payment support, affordable plan pricing
Timeline: Immediate — contract renewal negotiation in progress

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Payments / checkout: E-wallet support (not Stripe/credit card); manual enrollment by email with moderator team handling screenshot-based payment verification
Admin or seat management: Needs unlimited student capacity; currently managing by deleting inactive students
Special workflows or constraints: Payment collection happens entirely outside Teachable via E-wallets; moderator team handles verification manually

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "That's why I love teachable and I'm still with teachable and I didn't go to any other platform"
- Agreed to follow-up meeting on Thursday
- Open to reviewing custom plan proposal

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Price sensitivity: $12K/year is prohibitive; says he could build his own platform for a fraction
- Competitor leverage: Unnamed competitor offers pay-per-student at $0.75 with no subscription
- Payment method incompatibility: Audience cannot use credit cards; Stripe/Teachable Pay don't support E-wallets
- Student limit frustration: Was not aware of 5,000 student cap when subscribing

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Loves gamification, assignments, and certificates
- Wants E-wallet or mobile payment gateway integration
- Student limit was not clearly communicated during subscription

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth plan, currently ~$12K/year due to student overage
Discounts offered: Kevin proposed custom plan at ~$7,000 with unlimited students
Contract length discussed: Annual
Constraints or approvals needed: Jozeph wants to see formal proposal before committing

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Put together custom plan proposal with unlimited students at ~$7,000
- Send proposal via email
- Schedule follow-up meeting on Thursday

Customer:
- Review the custom plan proposal
- Meet again on Thursday to discuss

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Thursday (same week)
- Materials to send: Custom plan contract/proposal

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Jozeph is a passionate educator focused on accessibility, not profit maximization. He has significant social media reach (800k followers) and is converting followers to Teachable students. He genuinely likes the platform but is price-sensitive and has a legitimate payment infrastructure gap (E-wallets vs credit cards in Egypt). The unnamed competitor offering per-student pricing is a real risk.

calls.title: Alejandro Arriaga and Kevin Codde
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-02-12
ATTENDEES: Alejandro Arriaga (alejandro.arriaga@koltin.mx)
COMPANY: Koltin
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
Alejandro Arriaga from Koltin, a Mexican senior membership organization, is looking for a digital learning platform to extend their in-person community classes (yoga, painting, functional movement, etc.) to their nationwide membership base of 5,000-10,000 senior members. Key requirement is an intuitive, user-friendly interface since their audience lacks technical skills.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Digitize in-person community classes for nationwide senior membership
Audience: Senior citizens (membership-based), currently only 5% accessing in-person classes in Mexico City
Business model: Free courses included with membership (no commerce needed)
Content types: Video classes (yoga, painting, exercise, crafts), live coaching sessions, digital downloads/PDFs
Scale expectations: 30-40 courses, 10 instructors, 5,000-10,000 student members

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not yet established — Alejandro said "I don't have cost for this yet" but seemed receptive to $10K/yr
Authority: Alejandro is evaluating; needs to bring in Head of Experience and VP of Growth for final decision
Need: Strong — currently limited to in-person classes at one Mexico City location, company expanding nationwide
Timeline: "As soon as possible" — urgent but realistic about implementation time

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Admin or seat management: 10 instructors needing admin access, up to 15 admin users on Core plan
Special workflows or constraints: Must be extremely user-friendly for elderly non-technical users; Spanish-language support preferred for future sessions

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "I think you are a good option to us, to be honest"
- "That sounds really good" (after live coaching demo)
- "That's excellent. That's what I was looking for" (after progress tracking demo)
- Agreed to follow-up meeting next Thursday with additional stakeholders
- Plans to bring Head of Experience and VP of Growth to next meeting

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Budget not yet allocated — needs internal approval
- Decision requires buy-in from Head of Experience and VP of Growth
- Target audience (seniors) may struggle with technology adoption regardless of platform
- Language barrier — Alejandro's English is limited, may prefer Spanish going forward

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Core Internal Training ($10,000/year, ~$833/month)
Discounts offered: Kevin indicated flexibility of "a couple hundred dollars" if pricing is an issue
Contract length discussed: Annual plan presented
Constraints or approvals needed: Budget not yet defined internally

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send email recap with plan breakdown and pricing by end of day
- Schedule follow-up meeting for Thursday (Feb 20) at same time

Customer:
- Share email recap with Head of Experience and VP of Growth
- Bring stakeholders to Thursday follow-up meeting

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Thursday Feb 20, 2026 (same time)
- Materials to send: Email with plan details and pricing

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Alejandro seems genuinely interested and gave multiple positive signals throughout the demo. The fact that he's bringing VP of Growth and Head of Experience to the next call suggests real intent. Language barrier may slow communication but doesn't appear to be a blocker. Koltin is a growing company in Mexico expanding beyond Mexico City.

---

calls.title: ines gerardi and Zach McCall
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-02-10
ATTENDEES: Ines Gerardi (+ colleague)
COMPANY: Fundacion Flor
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Fundacion Flor is an Argentinian foundation that has been running in-person courses on leadership, finance, and related topics for 10 years. They want to create a virtual campus / online academy to expand their audience beyond Argentina and create a new revenue stream by selling courses online. This was a first demo call; Zach walked them through Teachable's course builder, embedding, community, coaching/webinars, organizations, quizzes, and pricing.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Create an online academy to sell existing course content (leadership, finance) to a broader audience
Audience: Current Argentinian students + new international/Latin American learners, plus B2B sales to companies
Business model: Sell courses online (one-time purchase, subscriptions, or memberships), also sell bulk seats to companies
Content types: Video courses (10-30 min segments), quizzes, possibly live webinars
Scale expectations: Starting with 1-2 courses, expanding over time

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Discussed $6,000/yr (Valentine's promo) or $5,500/yr (2-year commitment). Foundation needs internal approval for investment.
Authority: Ines and colleague are researching platforms; decision goes to their boss. They cannot commit on the call.
Need: Strong. They have 10 years of content and want to digitize and expand reach. Currently no online platform.
Timeline: Slow. They are in research phase, looking at multiple platforms. Follow-up scheduled for March 17.

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Embedding courses into their existing website
Reporting needs: Organization-level reporting (seat usage for B2B sales)
Payments / checkout: Multi-currency support (Argentine peso), Stripe integration, flexible pricing (one-time, subscription, payment plan)
Admin or seat management: Organization seat management for B2B corporate sales
Special workflows: B2B course sales with seat allocation, community per course

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Enthusiastic about platform capabilities (embedding, organizations, quizzes, community)
- Have 10 years of content ready to adapt
- Interested in B2B sales via organizations feature
- Scheduled follow-up for March 17
- Asked for Latin American customer references

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Still in research phase, evaluating multiple platforms
- Need internal approval from boss (foundation leadership)
- Timeline is slow (March follow-up at earliest)
- Foundation investment decision involves many stakeholders and strategic discussions
- Competitive market in Argentina for online courses

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Embedding capability is important for their existing website
- Organization seat management is critical for their B2B model
- Multi-currency (Argentine peso) support is essential
- Quiz/assessment features are needed
- Want account manager guidance on content strategy (video length, course structure)

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Likely the plan starting at $6,000/yr
Discounts offered: Valentine's discount ($6,000 vs $6,500), 2-year commitment ($5,500/yr)
Contract length discussed: 1-year or 2-year
Constraints: Foundation budget approval needed

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Send recap email with platform overview and capabilities
- Provide student-side demo/experience access
- Ask product team for Latin American (ideally Argentinian) customer references

Customer:
- Internal discussions about business model and platform choice
- Communicate platform capabilities to their boss
- Start adapting content for online format

Scheduled:
- Follow-up meeting March 17, 2026

Fadi also planning a new higher-ticket online school for summer 2026.

Kevin: Put together retention deal (pricing + unlimited admins), email Fadi

calls.title: Teachable <> Speravita
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-02
ATTENDEES: Jennifer Roush (Director, Speravita), Kristina Edelman (Operations, Speravita), Liselle (Training Coordinator, Speravita), Zach McCall (Teachable), Lennie Zhu (Teachable Product)
COMPANY: Speravita
STAGE: Evaluation / Follow-up Demo

---
SUMMARY
Follow-up call with Speravita team (100+ centers). Lennie Zhu from Teachable product team demoed new organization admin features: center point-of-contact can enroll students (up to seat limit), view progress reports and leaderboards, download quiz score CSVs, but cannot remove students or edit org settings. Three training tracks for different user roles (learner, patient representative, etc.). Jennifer is the decision-maker with board approval. They sell seat-based training: initial fee for 3 trainees, additional trainees at separate fee. Need content by May 1 for June class. Discussed access duration per product/bundle, compliance quiz settings, and org admin permissions. Follow-up in 2 weeks (week of March 16) with pricing.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Training platform for 100+ centers with seat-based enrollment
Audience: Healthcare/professional trainees across 100+ partner centers
Content types: Courses with quizzes, CEU-style training, bundled by role track
Business model: Seat-based B2B sales to centers (initial fee + per-trainee add-ons)
Scale: 100+ centers, 3 training tracks per center

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Board approval already granted
- Jennifer is decision-maker
- May 1 deadline for content readiness (June class incoming)
- Follow-up in 2 weeks with pricing
- Already had multiple demo calls with Teachable

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Send pricing proposal, schedule follow-up for week of March 16
Jennifer/team: Review pricing, prepare for onboarding

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Organization Hierarchy (~06:00) - 100+ centers, each with own admin point of contact
- Seat Management (~14:00) - Per-center seat allocation, billing tracking when seats added
- Organization-level Reporting (~13:00) - Center-level progress tracking and leaderboards
- Course Sequencing / Completion Gating (~13:30) - Prevent quiz skipping, enforce content completion
- Access Duration / Expiration (~17:00) - Different access durations per product/bundle
- Role-based Access (~14:00) - Org admin permissions (enroll but not remove students)
---

ATTENDEES: Alessandro Provera (Agency Owner, Italy), Zach McCall (Teachable)

---
SUMMARY
Discovery call with Alessandro Provera who runs a digital agency in Italy working with major food influencers (~1M+ followers). They produced a 6-episode professional pizza-making course with TV production quality. Strategy: sell at high volume, low price (~59 EUR Italy, $79-89 US/UK) to build a fan base. Community: 1M Instagram, 60K emails (Klaviyo), 10K WhatsApp (managed via Charles, a Dutch platform). Architecture: custom-coded landing page -> Teachable checkout -> course delivery. Audience: Food enthusiasts, Italian market primary, expanding to US/UK
Content types: 6-episode video course (TV production quality)

Scale: 1M Instagram, 60K email list, 10K WhatsApp community

Zach: Send API documentation, recap email, check on technical help scoping
Alessandro: Analyze plans with team, review API docs, reconnect next Friday

CALL DATE: 2026-02-26
ATTENDEES: Erica Fleischer (Program Coordinator, SNAP Training Program), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: SNAP Job Readiness Training program (Illinois, philanthropic-funded)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Demo call with Erica Fleischer about a job readiness training program for SNAP participants (able-bodied adults without dependents) in Illinois. Participants must complete 80 hours/month of work activity to maintain benefits. Program needs minimum 80 hours of job readiness training content at 8th-grade reading level with monthly reporting. Universe of 300,000 potential participants, realistic estimate ~10,000. Currently funded by a philanthropic group; state of Illinois would eventually procure. Target launch May 1st or sooner. Key gap: Erica wants platforms that come WITH pre-made content, not just a course-building tool. Rates Teachable "probably not that high" because the state already has an LMS under contract and other options include bundled content. Pro plan discussed at $10,000/year (10,000 students), scaling to ~$20,000/year at 300,000. Decision next week.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Job readiness training for SNAP participants to maintain benefits
Audience: SNAP recipients (able-bodied adults without dependents), 10,000-300,000 potential users
Content types: Videos (some from YouTube), quizzes, PDFs, resume-building exercises
Business model: Free to participants, funded by philanthropy/state government
Compliance: 80 hours/month SNAP requirement, monthly reporting by participant
Scale: 10,000 realistic start, 300,000 universe

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Urgency: May 1st launch target, "potentially sooner"
- Actively evaluating multiple providers
- Team decision meeting tomorrow
- BUT: Erica said Teachable "probably not that high" on their list
- Competitor advantage: other LMS options include pre-made content

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin: Send written proposal for Pro package ($10K/yr) and enterprise tier ($20K/yr), check Illinois procurement partnerships
Erica: Present to team tomorrow, decision by next week

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Completion Tracking (~03:00) - Monthly reporting for SNAP hour requirements
- Learning Paths (~06:00) - Suggested course paths to hit 80 hours, partial credit
- File Upload & Grading (~14:00) - Student resume creation within courses
- Seat Management (~19:00) - Reassign licenses when participants drop out

CALL DATE: 2026-02-25
ATTENDEES: Carolyn Castro (Trinity Church), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Trinity Church
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Discovery/demo call with Carolyn Castro from Trinity Church (staff of 30-40, ~300-400 volunteers). They want an online platform for volunteer training, discipleship tracks, and classes. Key needs: ministry-specific course organization (not all volunteers see all content), completion tracking, AI-assisted course creation, community features for online classes, and content drip. Kevin demonstrated organizations, course building, AI generation, communities, bundles, and certificates. Pricing discussed: Core internal training package at $5,000/year with 10% nonprofit discount. Carolyn needs boss approval before proceeding. Kevin offering trial link.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Online discipleship, volunteer onboarding, and training resource hub
Audience: 300-400 church volunteers across different ministries
Content types: Training videos, documents, quizzes
Business model: Free internal training (no sales intent currently)
Scale: Staff of 30-40, 20-25 admin users needed

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin: Send written proposal with trial link
Carolyn: Discuss with supervisor, potential follow-up call next week

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Group Enrollment (~05:00) - Ministry-specific course access
- Completion Tracking (~02:30) - Track who's watching and engagement
- Bulk User Import (~03:00) - 25 admin users creating content
- AI Course Generation (~12:00) - Help creating new courses from ideas/summaries
- Drip / Timed Content Release (~14:00) - Weekly course rollout
- Community Features (~13:00) - Discussion boards for online classes
- Content Templates (~13:00) - Faster course creation workflow
---

Choices & Community Living is an Ohio nonprofit with ~275 employees (34-36% annual turnover) providing care services. They need an LMS for internal staff training across 7 positions, primarily Direct Support Professionals (DSPs). They already evaluated Teachable through a partner organization (19 Services, 9-10 year relationship) and met with Matt Horner previously. They also evaluated Study Fetch but it was too expensive and had HIPAA concerns. They plan to create 40-50 thin-slice courses (~20 min modules) with quizzes and completion gating. Trent explicitly said "We're definitely going to buy" and will decide which plan within days.

Primary goal: Internal staff training LMS for 7 position types

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-02-25
ATTENDEES: Keith Schneringer (Marketing Lead, Waxie), Zach McCall (Teachable)
COMPANY: Waxie (janitorial/sanitary supply company, acquired)
STAGE: Decision / Ready to Buy

---
SUMMARY
Demo call with Keith Schneringer from Waxie, a janitorial/sanitary supply company that was acquired. Keith is in charge of marketing for their Jansan customers. Their previous LMS (set up in early 2000s, had 4,000 seats) was discontinued for financial reasons. Customers keep asking for training content. Short-term: stand up a platform with 12 courses for a school district (75 custodians) by March 12 for evaluation. Mid-term: go live July 1. Long-term: expand to other customers. Needs courses, quizzes, certificates, completion tracking, organizations for B2B, white label, gamification. Zach demonstrated AI course creation, organizations, compliance settings, certificates. Premium plan discussed at $6,500/year (or $6,000/year with 2-3 year commitment). Keith wants to make a decision by Friday and start building courses next week.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Customer training LMS for custodians at school districts and companies
Audience: Custodial staff at customer organizations (first client: 75 custodians at one school district)
Content types: 12 courses initially, SOPs, icons/graphics (avoiding dated video), quizzes, job cards
Business model: Primarily value-added service; potential to monetize for deeper training content
Scale: Previous LMS had 4,000 seats; initial deployment 75 custodians, scaling to multiple clients

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "What I'm looking to do is make a decision by tomorrow, Friday latest."
- Wants to start course creation next week
- School district deadline March 12 for evaluation, July 1 go-live
- Already spoke with Jerome (SDR) previously
- Asking detailed pricing and timeline questions
- Previous LMS discontinued, customers actively requesting training

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Send sandbox account and student-side demo account, recap over email, check in Friday
Keith: Evaluate sandbox, make plan decision by Friday, begin course creation next week

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- AI Course Generation (~19:00) - Has SOPs ready, interested in AI-assisted course creation
- Organization Hierarchy (~09:00) - Multiple school districts and companies as separate organizations
- Completion Tracking (~04:00) - Supervisors assign and track custodian course completion
- Certificate Automation (~04:30) - Certificates of completion for custodians
- Quiz Question Types (~04:00) - Knowledge checks with existing question library
- White Label (~16:00) - Interested in white label app for future
- Gamification (~04:00) - Reward learning milestones
- Seat Management (~25:00) - Previous LMS had 4,000 seats, needs scalable seat model
- Custom Domain (~17:00) - Custom URL for the learning platform
- Digital Downloads (~08:00) - Job cards and product information PDFs
- Video Scrub Prevention (~04:00) - Course compliance settings for video completion
---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-02-25
ATTENDEES: Tobie Ashiyana (Founder, Retreat Center), Zach McCall (Teachable)
COMPANY: Tobie Ashiyana Retreat Center (Spain-based)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Discovery/demo call with Tobie Ashiyana, who runs a retreat center in Spain offering live in-person retreats (e.g., "Transformation") with coaching alongside. Currently managing ~20 WhatsApp communities for retreat cohorts (growing 10 per year). Needs: coaching platform (1:1 and 1:many), community for each retreat cohort plus a central alumni community, online guide/coach training course, and a white label app. Key gaps identified: no in-app messaging for coaching (only via community DMs), no built-in calendar for coaching sessions (uses Calendly), no call logging for coach invoicing. Discussed white label app customization options (in-app messaging, calendar possible). Tobie also interested in assigning "rituals" (daily habits/behaviors) to clients via the app. Has multiple coaches on staff. Follow-up scheduled for next week after Zach checks with app development team.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Online coaching platform + community for retreat center alumni and cohort groups
Audience: Retreat attendees, coaching clients, yoga training students
Content types: Coaching sessions (1:1 video), courses (guide/coach training), community, meditations (audio/video)
Business model: Paid retreats + coaching packages + potential online course sales
Scale: ~20 community groups currently, growing 10/year; yoga training school

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Follow up on white label app customization questions (in-app messaging, calendar, custom features), send recap email
Tobie: Evaluate answers, reconnect next week

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Community Features (~03:00) - Replace WhatsApp with platform communities for retreat cohorts
- White Label (~03:30) - White label app for branded experience
- Direct Messaging (~05:00) - In-app messaging between coaches and clients
- Hybrid Scheduling (~12:00) - In-platform calendar for coaching session bookings
- Role-based Access (~20:00) - Multi-coach architecture, assigning coaches to specific clients
- Coaching Session Tracking (~20:30) - Log coaching calls for invoicing purposes
---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-02-24
ATTENDEES: Songwoot / James (Prospect, Hong Kong/Panama), Zach McCall (Teachable)
COMPANY: Songwoot IT Services (unnamed IT services company)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Discovery call with Songwoot (goes by James), who runs an IT services company based in Hong Kong for 10 years (~$2-3M annual revenue). They are relocating to Panama due to concerns about Chinese government intervention in Hong Kong financial services. The company serves primarily Japanese expatriates living worldwide and sells three products: cloud storage, collectible Japanese literature/manga, and Japanese architectural drawings. Songwoot wants to use Teachable primarily for selling Japanese literature and manga as digital content (PDFs). Zach demonstrated the platform, showed PDF hosting in course format, discussed pricing options (one-off, membership, download), and offered a sandbox account for testing. Follow-up scheduled for same time next Tuesday.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Sell Japanese literature and manga as digital content (PDFs) on a subscription/one-off basis
Audience: Japanese expatriates worldwide
Content types: PDF literature, manga, possibly architectural drawings
Business model: One-off purchases and/or annual subscriptions for digital content access
Scale: ~$2-3M annual revenue business, 10 years operating

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Payment processing: Needs Panama-compatible payment gateway (Stripe/PayPal)
Content format: PDF hosting and viewing (not page-flip, vertical scroll is acceptable)
Pricing: One-off purchase, annual subscription, and download options
Community: Interest in community features for Japanese content discussions

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Send sandbox/test account link
Songwoot: Test platform with PDF uploads, explore PayPal/Stripe for Panama
Follow-up: Same time next Tuesday

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- PDF Content Hosting (~08:00) - "If we have all those literatures already in PDF files"
- Guest Checkout (~15:00) - "Do they have to create their own account or they can just click on the product and buy it right away?"
- International Payment Processing (~18:00) - "Do you have the payout in Panama?"
- Digital Downloads (~14:00) - one-off downloadable purchases
- Community Features (~06:00) - "The Japanese would love it to have their own community"
- Membership / Subscription Pricing (~13:00) - annual subscription access model
---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-09
ATTENDEES: Rick Johnson (Refinery Pass), Kyle @RefineryPass (Refinery Pass), Zach McCall (zach.mccall@teachable.com), Lennie Zhu (Teachable)
COMPANY: Refinery Pass
STAGE: Demo / Technical Scoping

---
SUMMARY
Refinery Pass provides safety training for contractors at refineries across the US. Currently on Docebo, looking to migrate to Teachable. 50K+ student database, 60+ courses. Key challenge is managing contractor workforce that moves between companies and refineries. Need badging verification, organization-level management, and bulk purchasing. Deep technical scoping call with Lennie Zhu on organizations feature.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Refinery safety training and credentialing for contractors
Audience: 50K+ contractors at refineries across US (Ohio, Utah, Texas, North Dakota)
Business model: B2B training sold per-seat to contractor companies, plus individual purchases
Content types: MP4 video courses (basic refinery orientation + site-specific training)
Scale expectations: 50K+ students, 60+ products, thousands of bulk transactions per year

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Currently paying significantly more with Docebo. Open to 10-15K for custom development work.
Authority: Rick Johnson (decision maker), Kyle (technical lead)
Need: Migrate from Docebo. Need organization management, badging verification, bulk purchasing, AI tutor
Timeline: Ready to pull the trigger. Meeting with Maxime this week for AI tutor and custom work scoping.

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: API for custom purchasing flows, AI tutor/support agent (Maxime building)
Reporting needs: Student progress lookup by name/email, completion verification for badging
Payments / checkout: Bulk seat purchasing (credit card preferred, some invoicing), flexible seat quantities
Admin or seat management: Custom roles for badging offices (read-only all students), organization admins for companies
Special workflows or constraints: Workers move between companies frequently, need credential portability. Account merging for duplicate emails. Badging offices need global student search regardless of organization.

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "I think we're ready to pull the trigger."
- "I wish where were you guys six years ago when I needed you."
- "We're very motivated to make this work."
- Already tested sandbox account and liked it
- Open to custom development budget

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Bulk purchasing flow not yet available (Q2-Q3 roadmap)
- Organizations may be too heavyweight for small one-off contractor companies
- Workers using different emails creates identity management challenges

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth plan (or higher for bulk import)
Discounts offered: Significant savings vs Docebo pricing
Contract length discussed: Not specified
Constraints or approvals needed: Custom work quote from Maxime (10-15K range)

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-06
ATTENDEES: Cristina Collado (Plus Grade), Zach McCall (zach.mccall@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Plus Grade (formerly Okie, recently acquired)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Plus Grade provides hotel upselling software. They use free courses to train hotel front desk agents on upselling techniques and tool usage. Currently on Thinkific but forced to leave due to cybersecurity concerns flagged during acquisition due diligence. Low course revenue (~EUR 1,000 in 4 years). Based in the Netherlands.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Train hotel clients on upselling techniques and software usage
Audience: Hotel front desk agents and managers
Business model: Free courses for customers (100% discount codes), courses priced to deter competitors
Content types: Pre-recorded video courses with sequential completion
Scale: Small course catalog, customer-facing training

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed in detail. Pricing presented at $6,500/yr (2yr discount at $6,000/yr)
Authority: Cristina is evaluating. Must present shortlist to manager, then procurement.
Need: Replace Thinkific due to cybersecurity issue from acquisition. Need progress reporting for hotel managers.
Timeline: ASAP. Manager on holiday, reconnect week of March 16.

---
RISKS
- Unknown cybersecurity issue that caused Thinkific departure. Could affect Teachable too.
- Recently acquired by larger company. Procurement process unknown and potentially slow.
- Very low course revenue. Primary value is customer enablement, not direct revenue.

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Send recap, pricing, sales deck, test account, Teachable U student access.
Customer: Clarify cybersecurity issue, present shortlist to manager.
Scheduled: Follow-up Friday March 16 week.

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-05
ATTENDEES: Chavonne D. Stewart (Rehoboth Fellowship International), Kevin Codde (kevin.codde@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Rehoboth Fellowship International
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Nonprofit ministry launching Rehoboth Fellowship Bible Institute. Starting with 5-10 continuing education courses in August 2026, with a 12-year vision to build a full seminary college. Expecting 50-75 students in year one with 10% annual growth. Charging for courses with member vs non-member pricing. Currently using Wix for website.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Launch Bible Institute offering religious studies courses with certifications
Audience: Fellowship members and external students (50-75 year one)
Business model: Paid courses with tiered pricing (member discount vs non-member rate)
Content types: Pre-recorded video, live virtual sessions (hybrid), audio, quizzes
Scale: 5-10 courses initially, growing to full seminary over 12 years

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed. Builder plan at $69/mo recommended as starting point.
Authority: Chavonne is evaluator. Dr. Brian Hodges is visionary/decision-maker (not on call).
Need: LMS for Bible Institute launch. Courses, certs, badges, live sessions, community.
Timeline: Go-live August 2026. One more evaluation meeting next week, then decision.

---
RISKS
- Decision-maker (Dr. Hodges) was not on the call.
- Very small initial student base (50-75). May not justify higher-tier plans.
- 12-year growth vision. Current needs are modest.

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin: Follow up with contact info.
Customer: Share info with team, one more meeting next week, then decide.

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-05
ATTENDEES: Lauren Bendersky (Grapevine), Kevin Codde (kevin.codde@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Grapevine
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Grapevine is a medical supply ordering platform for practices. Strong retention but struggling with early adoption. Sales teams work with account admins, but end users (shoppers) don't get adequate onboarding. Currently using Scribe ($28/mo) for step-by-step guides but lack tracking/completion data. Exploring LMS for structured customer onboarding. Key requirement is embedding into their web platform via iframe with SSO.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Structured onboarding for end users (shoppers) of their supply ordering platform
Audience: ~500 current users, primarily new customers going forward
Business model: Free internal/customer training (not selling courses)
Content types: Screenshots, product walkthroughs, video, quizzes
Scale: ~500 existing users, focus on new customer onboarding

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: No set budget. Currently paying $28/mo for Scribe. Company willing to invest to solve early adoption problem.
Authority: Lauren is evaluator. Must present comparison to team.
Need: Structured onboarding to improve early adoption. Tracking completion. Embedding into platform.
Timeline: 30 days to make a decision. Discovery phase, meeting multiple vendors.

---
RISKS
- Embedding/iframe is a critical requirement. Not currently supported (on roadmap). Kevin to follow up.
- Evaluating multiple competitors. Teachable was first demo. 3-4 more demos same day.
- Enterprise pricing may be too high for ~500 user base. Needs SMB discount.
- No set budget established.

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin: Follow up on iframe/embedding question, send pricing with potential SMB discount.
Customer: Complete remaining vendor demos, compare and present to team.

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-05
ATTENDEES: Josh Nick (Emerging See Response), Kevin Codde (kevin.codde@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Emerging See Response
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Fire alarm contractor with ~25 technicians looking to build an employee training program. Currently doing on-the-job training only. Interested in onboarding curriculum, certifications, and quizzes. Standard demo call. Prospect expressed uncertainty about fit given company size vs. platform scale.

---
USE CASE
Internal employee training for fire alarm technicians. New hire onboarding and upskilling existing techs. Content would be video, text, and PDF. Certification tracking for required credentials.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed beyond pricing shown ($5K/yr Core plan)
Authority: Josh Nick appears to be decision-maker
Need: Training program for 25 technicians, 3-6 new hires/year
Timeline: Currently building content, no firm deadline

---
RISKS
- Prospect said "I'm not sure if this is the right fit" at end of call
- Small team size (25 techs) may not justify platform cost
- No urgency or timeline commitment

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin to send pricing in writing. Prospect to review and decide if fit.

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-05
ATTENDEES: Thomas Grobost (Swiss Job Board), Zach McCall (zach.mccall@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Swiss Job Board (name not disclosed)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Swiss job board company (near-monopoly in Switzerland) wants to offer free recruitment training courses to B2B customers and prospects as a marketing/lead-gen tool. ~100K businesses on platform. Key requirements are SSO integration and white-label embedding. Content is video, quizzes, PDFs. Free courses to drive job ad sales. Technical feasibility (SSO, embedding) is the primary evaluation gate.

---
USE CASE
Free recruitment training courses for B2B job board customers. Target audience: non-HR professionals at small-to-mid companies who need to learn hiring best practices. Courses as lead magnet to drive job ad purchases. Content: video, quizzes, PDF documents.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Pricing discussed at $7,500/yr (or $7K for 2-year commitment)
Authority: Thomas is evaluating, needs to share with internal team and legal
Need: Free course platform embedded in existing job board with SSO
Timeline: Want something live before June 2026

---
RISKS
- SSO integration complexity is the primary blocker
- Need SOC 2 documentation (requires NDA)
- Internal buy-in needed from tech and legal teams
- 100K businesses means organizations feature may not scale for their use case

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach to send: pricing recap, example school websites, Teachable U access, one-pager/deck, SSO documentation, SOC 2 (after NDA). Follow-up call scheduled March 19.

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-04
ATTENDEES: Steve Kinney (Steve Kinney Audio), Zach McCall (zach.mccall@teachable.com), Jerome Olaloye (jerome.olaloye@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Steve Kinney Audio
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Audio production educator with long-form 4K video courses (mixing, editing in Pro Tools/Luna). Main concern is large file sizes (courses up to 1.2TB, individual files up to 67GB). Interested in tiered membership/community, private video hosting, SSO with Discord and Shopify, and Shopify integration. Currently uses YouTube (unlisted) for member videos and Shopify for commerce. Exploring Teachable for courses, community, and memberships.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Sell audio production courses and tiered community memberships
Audience: Audio engineers and producers ("pinky out" quality expectations)
Business model: Course sales (currently via Shopify) + planned tiered membership (free/paid/premium)
Content types: Long-form 4K video demonstrations of DAW workflows (Pro Tools, Luna, DaVinci Resolve)
Scale expectations: 2 courses done, 2 more planned. First course ~1.2TB, second ~300GB (compressible to ~100GB)

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Evaluating Growth plan, open to enterprise if storage needs require it. Proposed YouTube ad read partnership to offset costs.
Authority: Steve is sole decision maker.
Need: Large file hosting, tiered community, private video hosting, Shopify or SSO integration.
Timeline: Follow-up call next Monday. Working on compressing files in the meantime.

---
RISKS
- 2GB per-file upload limit may be a hard blocker (individual files 25-67GB pre-compression)
- May need enterprise pricing for storage (multi-terabyte potential)
- Locked into Shopify with existing mailing list and conversion data
- Video embedding limitations in native community

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Check if 2GB file limit is bypassable. Investigate Discord SSO and Shopify SSO options. Check on ad read partnership possibility. Provide sandbox account. Follow up next Monday.
Steve: Compress all course files via Handbrake to determine actual storage needs. Assess file sizes.

---

CALL DATE: 2026-03-03
ATTENDEES: Rick Johnson (Refinery Pass), Kyle Jones (Refinery Pass), Zach McCall (zach.mccall@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Refinery Pass
STAGE: Follow-up Demo / Technical Validation

---
SUMMARY
Follow-up call with Refinery Pass (refinery safety training, 50K+ students). Rick and Kyle are validating remaining concerns after watching a demo video twice. Key topics: course expiration for compliance, custom enrollment fields (birthday for identity), AI support chatbot to eliminate 5AM customer service, white label app, Shopify integration, seat reassignment, and browser compatibility. Very strong buying signals. Rick estimates 90% cost savings vs Docebo ($60K/yr). Targeting Docebo contract end (March 31) for migration. Planning to meet with Lenny on organizations feature next week.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Refinery safety training and credentialing for contractors
Audience: Blue collar contractors at refineries across US
Business model: B2B training sold per-seat to contractor companies via Shopify, plus individual purchases
Current pain: Subscription code fulfillment requires 5AM customer support; SCORM/Safari bugs; Docebo at $60K/yr with limited support
Scale: 50K+ student database, ~2K new students/month, 60+ courses

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Currently paying ~$60K/yr for Docebo. Teachable at ~$6,500/yr. Open to AI chatbot add-on ($8-15K one-time).
Authority: Rick Johnson (decision-maker), Kyle Jones (technical lead)
Need: Eliminate subscription code fulfillment, course expiration, seat reassignment, browser compatibility, mobile app
Timeline: Docebo quarterly contract due March 31. Six-week window to migrate. Decision expected before Friday.

---
RISKS
- Breaking Docebo contract may cause friction ("it's gonna get messy")
- Currently using Shopify for checkout, need API/webhook bridge until Q4 migration
- Organizations feature still being built (need early access)
- No custom enrollment fields for birthday/identity disambiguation

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth plan (~$6,500/yr)
AI chatbot: $8-15K one-time custom build
White label app: $4-8K one-time
Docebo comparison: $60K/yr current spend

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: Set up meeting with Lenny (organizations product team) for Monday/Tuesday. Scope AI support chatbot. Send sandbox account. Investigate extending trial period.
Rick/Kyle: Test sandbox. Make migration decision before Friday. Meet with Lenny re: organizations.

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "I didn't see a problem to begin with. And after this conversation, I really don't see problem."
- "This is probably damn near perfect solution for what we are at."
- "I wish we had this opportunity to have this conversation about six years ago."
- Targeting decision before Friday, Docebo contract end March 31

---

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-20
ATTENDEES: Rachel Costa, Daniel Ramalhosa
COMPANY: [NEEDS IDENTIFICATION - nonprofit learning org serving changemakers]
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
Nonprofit learning organization that offers async and live learning to nonprofit changemakers. They recently acquired a company using Docebo and currently use Contentful for async content. Rebuilding their application and evaluating LMS options on a 1-2 month timeline. Foundation partners (e.g., Sterling) enroll nonprofit orgs in their programs.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Unified LMS for async courses, coaching, and community for nonprofit changemakers
Audience: Nonprofit organizations and changemakers, mostly US-based with some global
Business model: Mix of free and paid learning; foundation-sponsored access
Content types: Courses (hundreds of SCORM/xAPI files), coaching (10 coaches), community, surveys
Scale expectations: Multiple foundation partners with 20+ orgs each

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Discussed $7,500/yr base + $5,000 SSO = ~$12K/yr; noted Docebo is too expensive
Authority: Rachel and Daniel making joint decision, meeting in 1 hour to discuss
Need: High - actively rebuilding platform, have content ready to migrate
Timeline: Framework in 1-2 weeks, users in 1-2 months

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: SSO (required), API for data exchange with their platform, SurveyMonkey embed
Reporting needs: Per course, per student, per organization reporting; API access to data
Payments / checkout: Mix of free and paid access, coupon-based free coaching sessions, memberships vs bundles
Admin or seat management: Organizations for foundation partners, team admins
Special workflows or constraints: Need SCORM + xAPI support (hundreds of files to migrate), learning paths for course sequencing, community spaces per foundation

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Meeting internally in 1 hour to discuss LMS options
- Active timeline: 1-2 months to launch
- Already rebuilding their application
- Docebo too expensive, looking for alternatives
- Deep technical questions showing real evaluation

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- SCORM not available until Q3 (they have hundreds of files)
- Learning Paths not available until Q3
- xAPI status unclear
- Monthly recurring coupon use not supported natively

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Enterprise at $7,500/yr + $5,000 SSO = ~$12,000/yr
Discounts offered: $500/yr discount for 2+ year commitment ($7,000/yr)
Contract length discussed: Multi-year option mentioned
Constraints or approvals needed: Internal discussion between Rachel and Daniel

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Send recap email with pricing and details
- Follow up on xAPI availability
- Provide learning paths timeline details

Customer:
- Internal discussion (same day)
- Follow up with decision on how to proceed

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-20
ATTENDEES: Edgar Gravel, Pierre Cloutier (IT Developer), Jesse (sync jlc, Berlin-based)
COMPANY: IAS Online (International Accreditation Service, subsidiary of ICC)
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
Existing Teachable customer (7+ years) on Advanced plan approaching 100-course limit. IAS provides training to laboratories worldwide on accreditation standards (FDA import/export, drinking water testing, etc.). Parent corp ICC scrutinizing their tech choices, demanding PCI compliance docs. Evaluating Enterprise upgrade for more courses, API access, account manager, and future features.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Scale training platform beyond 100 courses, add multilingual content (Spanish translations)
Audience: Laboratories globally (US, Africa, Asia) needing accreditation training
Business model: Free/public good training for lab accreditation (cost center, not revenue)
Content types: 27+ webinar-based courses (ELAP series), planning Synthesia AI video production
Scale expectations: 100+ courses, expanding to translated versions

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Favorable reaction to $5,000/yr (multi-year) vs current Advanced plan
Authority: Edgar (decision maker), Pierre (IT), Jesse (strategic/technical lead)
Need: High - approaching course limit, parent org pressure on compliance
Timeline: Active discussion, meeting with product lead (Jonathan) next Thursday

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: HubSpot, Zapier, custom webhooks, V2 API access, MCP/Claude integration
Reporting needs: Per-organization reporting, certificate tracking
Payments / checkout: Stripe (PCI compliance critical for parent corp ICC)
Admin or seat management: Organizations for occasional group enrollments (~2x/year)
Special workflows or constraints: Certificate PDF quality (800px rendering), course delisting with active certs, SCORM export for potential forced migration to ICC platform, multilingual course management

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- 7+ year loyal customer
- Favorable price reaction ($5K/yr multi-year)
- Scheduling meeting with product lead Jonathan
- President keeping parent corp pressure at bay
- Genuine need for more courses

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Parent corp ICC could force migration to their SCORM platform
- Jesse evaluating WordPress/LearnDash/WooCommerce as alternative
- Certificate PDF quality issues unresolved
- V2 API capabilities still unclear
- SCORM not available until Q3

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Enterprise at $6,000/yr base, $5,000/yr with multi-year commitment
Discounts offered: $1,000/yr off for 2+ year commitment
Contract length discussed: 2-3 year options
Constraints or approvals needed: Parent corp ICC oversight

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Get official PCI compliance documentation
- Schedule meeting with Jonathan (product lead) for Thursday
- Send recap email with pricing and Enterprise details
- Check on V2 API capabilities, xAPI, SCORM timing

Customer:
- Meet with Jonathan on learning paths and certificates
- Internal discussion on Enterprise vs alternatives

CALL DATE: 2026-03-19
ATTENDEES: Bryan Aho, Ibrahim Haleem Khan, Kess Kofi (Security), Priya (Logic Grain PM - listener)
COMPANY: DOT Compliance
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
DOT Compliance is migrating their driver compliance training from an existing LMS to Teachable with a July 1st go-live target. They need deep Salesforce integration for user provisioning, purchase flows, and certificate delivery to their DQFM (Driver Qualification File Management) system. Tom Lorimer (Teachable partner) is building the middleware bridge.

---

Primary goal: DOT driver compliance training with automated certificate delivery to DQFM audit system

---

Scott is Executive Director of AAMN, a professional association promoting men in nursing. Worked with ANA to create specialty certification in men's health nursing. October launch target.

Budget: Association (price-sensitive, mentioned affordability)

- Narrow choices by May 1

- Inquire about custom branded app capability
- Send growth plan proposal

Customer:
- Get Fluid Pay percentage rates
- Compare with other demo (same afternoon)
- Make decision within a week

CALL DATE: 2026-03-13
ATTENDEES: Maryland Vyagale
COMPANY: Vyagale Academy (Global Micro School)
STAGE: Discovery/Demo

---
SUMMARY
Maryland Vyagale is CEO/Founder of a global micro school/academy serving infants through corporate professionals. Has superintendent and legal background. Already has own custom LMS with gamification and AI built by her team, but shopping for additional/alternative platforms. Launching first in Mexico with teachers, then US, Spain (Salamanca), Dubai. Starting with 30-50 teachers and 40-50 courses. Courses are free for teachers to deliver; revenue from affluent clients, companies, and government entities (ESL training). Wants course licensing/bundle sales to school districts. Needs teacher-to-parent feedback capability. Kevin proposed core/enterprise package at $5,000/yr with 50 courses (bumped from 25), 2,500 students, 15 admins.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Startup - asked about installment payments ($416/mo)
Authority: Sole founder/CEO, makes all decisions
Need: Medium - already has own LMS, this is supplementary
Timeline: Mexican teachers launching this month

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send written proposal with pricing breakdown
- Include core package details (50 courses, $5K/yr)

Customer:
- Review proposal
- Coordinate with Mexico team on launch timing

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-03-13
ATTENDEES: Todd (Director of Officials), Clark Evans (Technical Lead), Tom Lorimer (Teachable Implementation Partner)
COMPANY: WIAA Officials (Washington state sports officiating)
STAGE: Technical Scoping / Implementation Planning

---
SUMMARY
Technical planning call for integrating Teachable with Arbiter (officiating eligibility management software). Currently using Brain Shark for course delivery with hourly data sync to Arbiter. Need: when an official completes a Teachable course, push completion data to Arbiter custom fields to update eligibility status. Tom Lorimer (Teachable implementation partner) will build bridge app. Plan to pilot with existing "What It Takes" course from Referee Enterprises (already on Teachable). Todd wants to duplicate/migrate this course to their own Teachable account. Will use Arbiter custom fields (binary completion: 0/1 or date) mapped to Teachable course/lecture IDs. Email-based user matching. Goal: prove concept this year, scale to full clinic system by 2027-28.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Open to custom build costs; existing Arbiter relationship
Authority: Todd is decision maker for officials program; Clark handles Arbiter technical side
Need: High - replacing Brain Shark integration with Teachable
Timeline: Pilot before next school year (officials start June/July); full scale 2027-28

- Coordinate Tom + Nate/Natty (Arbiter tech) meeting next week

- Be available for procurement questions

CALL DATE: 2026-03-29
ATTENDEES: Tom Lorimer (tom@purplehippo.io), zach.mccall@teachable.com, sarah.todd@unitehealth.com.au, Simon Davey (simon.davey@unitehealth.com.au)
COMPANY: Purplehippo

---
SUMMARY
- **LMS Transition:** Decision made to shift from Moodle to Teachable for better flexibility and cloud-based features.  
- **Scheduling Needs:** Complex course delivery models require advanced scheduling; Teachable currently lacks adequate support for in-person training.  
- **Custom Integration Proposal:** Plan to build an external scheduling app connected to Teachable via OAUTH and API to enhance functionality.  
- **Cost Estimates:** MVP development projected at €45,000 to €55,000; full build could reach €75,000 to €110,000, depending on features.  
- **Market Analysis:** No existing LMS adequately supports the hybrid training model, driving interest in custom solutions for competitive advantage.  
- **User Experience Focus:** Maintaining seamless integration on the main site is crucial for user satisfaction and operational efficiency.

Estimated 500 active monthly users to start, with plans for growth.

CALL DATE: Unknown
ATTENDEES: Andrea T (Imago Global Grassroots), Natalia Guerra-García (Imago Global Grassroots)
COMPANY: Imago Global Grassroots
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Nonprofit that delivers impact-scaling training courses to other NGOs, funded by a large foundation. Currently on SharePoint after migrating from Google Classroom and Educate Me. Want more interactive, visual course experience with community features, homework submissions, automated notifications, and organization-level reporting for ~10 NGOs per cohort.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Deliver impact-scaling course to other NGOs (run 1-2x/year for 6 years)
Audience: Other nonprofits/NGOs (10 orgs per cohort)
Business model: Foundation-funded, courses are free to participants
Content types: Live sessions, readings, group homework, working documents, recordings
Scale expectations: ~10 orgs per course, modest scale

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Cost-sensitive. Considering Builder plan ($89/mo) for just the months needed (4 months/year).
Authority: Andrea appears to be lead, Natalia supporting
Need: Platform with community, homework, organized modules, notifications
Timeline: This year

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Mural (for exercises, link only), Zoom (for live sessions), email (Mailchimp/Kit for automations)
Reporting needs: Per-student completion tracking, per-organization reporting
Payments / checkout: Not needed (free courses)
Admin or seat management: 10 organizations per course needing grouping

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Very cost-sensitive, may only subscribe 4 months/year
- May not need premium features
- Concern about losing course structure if subscription lapses

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Builder ($89/mo) or Growth ($1700/yr)
Discounts offered: Annual discount available
Contract length discussed: Monthly, potentially 4 months on/8 months off

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Provide discount code for annual plans

Customer:
- Evaluate Builder plan for seasonal use
- Decide on monthly vs annual subscription
---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Community Features - ""
- Direct Messaging - ""
- File Upload & Grading - ""
- Drip / Timed Content Release - ""
- Completion Tracking - ""
- Automated Email Sequences - ""
- Content Migration - ""
- Multi-Level Admin Hierarchy (Organizations) - ""

CALL DATE: Unknown
ATTENDEES: Zach McCall (Teachable), Joie Rhein (Prospect), Brittany Froistad (Prospect)
COMPANY: Two Red Beans (dating app partner) / Joie Rhein's education company
STAGE: Technical Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Joie Rhein and Brittany Froistad are building an educational offering that integrates with a dating app called Two Red Beans (60K MAU, 25K organic new users/month). They are currently on Thinkific and evaluating Teachable. The call was a technical requirements review based on a pre-submitted email list.

SCORM is the absolute go/no-go for this deal. Teachable's SCORM is still in internal development (not yet in customer beta). Joie stated they cannot sign without a working SCORM player. They only need complete/incomplete tracking from SCORM.

Other key requirements: SSO, webhooks to trusted URLs (high security, no third parties), HubSpot integration, automated workflows (event-triggered email/SMS), gated videos, quizzes, sales funnel analytics, high API rate limits, course embedding in apps/websites, surveys, and student progress tracking.

Next step: Zach to check with product team on SCORM timeline and report back. If SCORM is a go, next call would include Q (the dating app owner/head engineer) and a technical person.

CALL DATE: Unknown
ATTENDEES: Annie (Leiths Education)

---
SUMMARY
UK-based online cookery school with professional (6-month, 1500 GBP) and amateur (8-13 week) courses. Currently using Workshop platform whose contract ends October 2028. Core USP is mentored learning: cohorts of 10 students post food photos and get structured feedback from assigned mentors. Looking for a new platform that handles mentor-mentee interaction, content dripping, certificates, and commerce.

Primary goal: Replace Workshop platform for mentored cookery courses
Audience: Professional and amateur cooking students, international

Content types: Video lessons, step-by-step cooking instruction, mentor feedback on photos
Scale expectations: Cohorts of 10 per mentor, 4 mentors

---

Budget: Enterprise plan discussed at $7,500/yr, multi-year discount $500/yr off
Authority: Runs online arm, needs senior leadership approval
Need: Mentor-mentee interaction, content migration, certificates, drip scheduling
Timeline: Contract ends October 2028, wants to start evaluation early

---

Zach:

Customer:
- Present findings to senior leadership
- Decide on pilot approach

- Organizations & Multi-tenancy - ""

SUMMARY
Child and family health nursing practice in South Australia that performs government-funded developmental health checks on babies and children at childcare centers. ---

Australian startup building a network for commercial real estate agencies. Members get access to training via a portal. Plans to lease courses from Skillings Education and load them onto Teachable. Audience: Agency staff (2-3 per agency, ~20 agencies = ~60 users)
Business model: Mix of free (included in membership) and paid courses
Content types: Static PDFs, interactive short courses (25-30 min), video
Scale expectations: Starting with ~60 users across 20 agencies

Budget: Builder plan ($69/mo) with 10% coupon
Authority: Founder/decision-maker
Need: Course hosting, portal integration, quiz functionality
Timeline: Early stage, needs to coordinate with portal builder and course provider

NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send integration documentation and help site links
- Send 10% coupon code for Builder plan

Customer:
- Coordinate with portal builder for tab integration
- Contact Skillings Education about course loading
---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Organizations & Multi-tenancy - ""
- Assessments & Quizzes - ""
- Course Embedding - ""

CALL DATE: 2026-05-05
ATTENDEES: Jessica Miller-Merrell (Workology), Anna Damico (Teachable), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Workology
STAGE: Partnership Discussion

---
SUMMARY
Jessica Miller-Merrell, CEO of Workology and HR content creator, discussed a content partnership with Teachable. She has extensive existing training content (compliance, harassment, leadership, communication, progressive discipline) that she can modularize into 20-minute segments for Teachable's enterprise clients. Anna Damico presented Teachable's 'matchmaking' pilot program connecting content creators with enterprise buyers across three pillars: AI training, leadership/people management, and communication/productivity. Jessica's content aligns strongly with pillars two and three. Revenue model discussed as commission-based, with Teachable selling licenses and paying Jessica a percentage. Jessica offered to create exclusive Teachable-only versions of her content.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Content partnership -- supply modular HR/compliance training for Teachable enterprise clients
Audience: Enterprise employees, managers, new hires
Business model: Commission/revenue share on license sales through Teachable
Content types: Video presentations with slides, audio segments, quizzes, SCORM-compatible modules
Scale expectations: Starting with mini-course sample, expanding to full library of 10+ topic areas

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Revenue share model (percentage TBD)
Authority: Jessica is decision-maker for Workology content; Anna presenting to Teachable leadership in Brazil this week
Need: Enterprise clients need plug-and-play training content; Jessica needs distribution channel
Timeline: Two weeks for initial mini-course sample; filming cycle every six weeks

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Jessica has content ready or near-ready for most proposed topics
- Offered to create exclusive Teachable-only content
- Willing to support sales calls for large clients
- Already familiar with commission models from other learning providers
- Proactively proposed plug-and-play approach to minimize friction

---
NEXT STEPS
Teachable (Anna/Kevin):
- Present matchmaking pilot to leadership in Brazil
- Draft proposal with revenue share terms and roles/responsibilities
- Share prioritized topic list with Jessica
- Create Teachable account for Jessica
- Assign onboarding team member

Customer (Jessica):
- Review topic priorities from Teachable
- Build mini-course sample within two weeks
- Test Teachable platform for formatting/sizing needs
- Prepare exclusive content versions for Teachable

CALL DATE: Unknown
ATTENDEES: Autumn Zaminski (RIU)
COMPANY: Regional Intermediate Unit (RIU)
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Pennsylvania Intermediate Unit serving 25 school districts. Currently using PowerSchool and Schoology for PD. Wants to pilot Teachable for AI-focused asynchronous PD in 26-27 school year. Referred by Berks County IU (existing Teachable customer). Planning Builder plan ($89/mo) for pilot, then enterprise for org-wide rollout.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Asynchronous professional development for educators
Audience: Teachers across 25 school districts
Business model: Mix of free and paid PD courses, district contracts
Content types: AI training courses, async conference sessions
Scale expectations: One district pilot first, then 25+ districts

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Growth plan annual budgeted, starting with Builder at $89/mo
Authority: Associate Director, needs org-wide buy-in for enterprise
Need: Organizations, compliance, certificates, learning paths
Timeline: June 2026 pilot, 26-27 school year full rollout

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Flag support team for new account
- Notify when learning paths feature launches

Customer:
- Start Builder plan for June pilot
- Present results to leadership for enterprise decision
---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Organizations & Multi-tenancy - ""
- Personalized Learning Paths (Rules-Based) - ""
- Certificate Automation - ""
- Course Compliance Settings - ""
- Multi-Language Support - ""

CALL DATE: 2026-06-05

---
SUMMARY
PM Diplomas is a UK-based provider of postgraduate orthopedic surgery diploma programs (approximately 10 programs, each ~25 weeks). Currently on Moodle, they are building a new company and website with their first new program launching September 2026 and marketing starting late June. They evaluated Teachable as an all-in-one replacement covering white-label delivery, international VAT/merchant of record handling, and assessment tools.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Replace Moodle with a white-labeled all-in-one platform for postgraduate surgical diploma delivery
Audience: Orthopedic surgery trainees and qualified surgeons; paying delegates, 200-300 per cohort
Business model: One-time course/diploma purchase per program
Content types: Recorded Zoom lectures (PowerPoint-based), SBA question banks per lecture, extended essay finals
Scale expectations: ~10 diplomas with ~25 lectures each; September 2026 launch target

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not explicitly discussed; growth or premium plan likely ($6,500/yr quoted for premium at 50K students)
Authority: Sherief Elsayed is the primary decision-maker; Christopher Horton handles technical operations
Need: High — new company launch imminent in September, marketing starting late June
Timeline: Marketing starts late June 2026; platform launch September 2026

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Zoom (live sessions), Stripe + PayPal (payment processing)
Reporting needs: Per-course attendance and enrollment tracking; full delegate name/email data ownership
Payments / checkout: UK company selling to EU and Australia; critical requirement is MOR-based international VAT remittance with no double-taxation
Admin or seat management: Multiple faculty logins needed for distributed extended essay grading
Special workflows or constraints: Full white-label required; delegates log in from pmdiplomas.com; multi-faculty grading of extended essays needed

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Scheduled follow-up for Monday at the end of the call
- Sherief said 'super helpful' and 'very helpful please' in response to tax handling explanation
- Strong urgency driven by September launch with late June marketing start

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Merchant of record/VAT clarity is the key blocker — Sherief wants to avoid double-taxation on UK VAT when Teachable remits EU/global taxes; Zach could not confirm details on the call
- Distributed faculty grading for extended essays is unconfirmed as a Teachable capability — potential product gap
- No native live video streaming; Zoom runs externally (Sherief seemed mildly disappointed)
- Sherief has invested in their existing website and was concerned about having to rebuild the diploma workflow

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Multi-faculty grading/marking of extended essay assessments is needed but was not confirmed as supported

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth (5,000 students) and Premium (~$6,500/yr, 50,000 students)
Discounts offered: None
Contract length discussed: None
Constraints or approvals needed: Not discussed

NEXT STEPS
Zach:

- Book Monday 2026-06-08 at 1:00 PM ET follow-up call

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-26
ATTENDEES: Robin (Robin Springs LLC), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Robin Springs LLC
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
Robin is the owner of Robin Springs LLC, offering paid personal and professional community education courses (AI, grant writing, business proposals, emotional intelligence, hydroponics, canning, food sustainability) currently delivered via Zoom with PowerPoints and PDFs. She is evaluating Teachable to move to an asynchronous, platform-based course model with direct selling, targeting a September 2026 launch. She is cross-comparing Teachable against a few other LMS platforms.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Replace manual Zoom-based delivery with asynchronous self-hosted courses students can access anytime
Audience: General community / public learners; ~18 students per class, geographically dispersed (FL, CA, etc.)
Business model: Paid courses ($25–$35+ per course), sold directly to consumers; students register and pay per course
Content types: Video recordings, PowerPoints, PDFs; potential live sessions and digital downloads
Scale expectations: Starting small; evaluating Builder vs. Growth plan; September launch target

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Undecided between Builder and Growth plans; price-conscious but not objecting to cost
Authority: Sole owner and decision-maker
Need: High — no LMS today, entirely manual Zoom + PDF workflow
Timeline: September 2026 target launch

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Zoom (live sessions), Calendly (coaching/scheduling)
Reporting needs: Not discussed in depth
Payments / checkout: Wants to sell courses with no transaction fees; currently collects payment for Zoom events
Admin or seat management: Low priority at current scale
Special workflows or constraints: Wants plan flexibility to downgrade if needed; no long-term commitment preference; also teaches with Canvas/Blackboard at University of Bridgeport (separate, unrelated context)

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Proactively asked about AI course generation before the demo began, showing prior research across platforms
- Volunteered a September 2026 launch date unprompted
- Very positive throughout: "This was so, so good. Thank you so much for all of this."
- Engaged in detail on Builder vs. Growth trade-offs, product limits, and archiving — active evaluation behavior
- Confirmed she sells courses and collects payment, validating direct revenue use case
- Expressed that white-label branding is "actually important" to her

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Actively comparing Teachable against "a couple of other LMS platforms"
- Small scale (~18 students/class, $25–35/course) — deal size will be low; risk of choosing Builder without onboarding
- May opt for Builder plan (no white glove onboarding) to save cost

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Very positive reaction to AI course generation feature
- Liked the 2-week onboarding timeline estimate; excited by the ease of setup vs. Canvas/Blackboard
- Interested in removing Teachable branding (expressed it is "actually important")
- Asked good comparative questions about archiving and plan limits — shows platform literacy

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Builder and Growth (leaning between both)
Discounts offered: Kevin to send trial links with 10% discount on both plans
Contract length discussed: No annual commitment discussed; Robin specifically valued flexibility to change plans
Constraints or approvals needed: None — sole decision-maker

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send trial links for Builder and Growth plans (with 10% discount)
- Send recommendations on video recording tools clients use (to replace Zoom for async recording)

Customer:
- Sign up for trial and evaluate the platform
- Decide between Builder and Growth plans

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Not scheduled
- Materials to send: Trial links, video recording tool recommendations

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Robin is an enthusiastic, community-focused educator with broad course subject matter (tech and nature/sustainability). She is clearly the sole decision-maker with no internal approval hurdles. Her main friction with current tools (Canvas, Blackboard) is clunkiness and lack of AI to speed up course creation — Teachable's AI generator was a clear differentiator for her. Gut feel: warm lead, genuinely engaged, September timeline is real. Primary risk is ending up on Builder without onboarding support.
