calls.title: Connect to Teachable - Zach / Hannah
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-25
ATTENDEES: Hannah Shaw, Zach McCall (zmccall@teachable.com)
COMPANY: Hannah Shaw
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Hannah Shaw is a professional animal welfare educator and content creator with ~4 million social media followers, 11 books (including NYT bestsellers), and 450+ YouTube instructional videos on neonatal kitten care. She wants to launch structured online courses to create a scalable certification standard for foster parents and animal shelter professionals. She evaluated multiple platforms and told Zach that Teachable "by far seems like the right place."

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Build and sell self-paced online courses on kitten fostering and animal shelter professional skills; create an unofficial but standardized certification for foster caregivers
Audience: Consumer foster parents (large audience, ~4M social following); animal shelter staff and professionals
Business model: One-time course purchases (intro course ~$15; advanced course ~$100-200); potential bulk institutional licensing to shelters; possible future live Q&A cohort
Content types: New video recordings (based on existing workshops), PDFs, written modules, embedded YouTube clips, quizzes with pass thresholds
Scale expectations: Intro course could reach 10,000+ students; has 100K email subscribers and 4M social followers ready to notify; 437 Instagram pre-signups for advanced class already collected

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Comfortable with self-serve plans ($39-139/mo range); $6,500 custom plan is out of scope for now
Authority: Solo decision-maker; no approval needed
Need: High — has content, audience, and email list ready; expressed clear intent to proceed
Timeline: Plans to start on Starter monthly immediately; expects months to build content before publishing

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Already uses Squarespace (website) and Mailchimp (email); asked about embedding courses into Squarespace
Reporting needs: Quiz and survey result tracking with aggregated reporting in admin backend
Payments / checkout: Self-serve checkout; bulk institutional payment for shelters via custom coupon codes; ACH transfer mentioned for large shelter deals; asked about plan upgrade/downgrade flow
Admin or seat management: Concerned about seat caps; wants ability to delete inactive students; exploring org/admin features for shelters as a future-state need
Special workflows or constraints: Quiz pass thresholds (90% required); prerequisite gating (foundational course must be completed before advanced); content protection (no downloads); perpetual student access

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "Teachable by far seems like the right place for me" after evaluating multiple platforms
- "I definitely want to do it" at close of call
- Planning to sign up for Starter monthly immediately
- Has 100K email subscribers and 4M social audience ready to notify at launch
- 437 pre-signups from informal Instagram poll for advanced class
- Deep, specific questions about platform mechanics throughout the demo
- Already runs lead magnet / email capture on her Squarespace site; understood funnel concepts natively

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Time to create new video content is the primary bottleneck; she acknowledged this explicitly
- Uncertainty about right plan tier before knowing her actual student volume
- No hard launch deadline; could stay in build phase for an extended period

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Seat limits on other platforms were a key dealbreaker; Teachable's scalable enrollment was differentiating
- Persistent/unlimited access duration is essential for review-based content (animal care changes, people return)
- Wants native survey/data collection tool; Google embed workaround is a gap she noticed
- Bulk institutional licensing workflow (shelters buying seats at reduced rates) is an important channel she envisions
- Subtitles/translation feature (70 languages) resonated positively

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Starter monthly during build phase; Builder or Growth when ready to publish
Discounts offered: 10% off annual plan when she is ready to commit
Contract length discussed: Monthly to start; annual when comfortable with volume
Constraints or approvals needed: None

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Follow up when Hannah is ready to move to an annual plan
- Offer the 10% annual discount at that point

Customer:
- Sign up for Starter plan monthly
- Film new course content; organize existing PDFs, videos, and written materials into structured courses
- Notify 100K email list and social following at launch

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: None scheduled; Hannah will self-direct
- Materials to send: None specified

ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Hannah Shaw is a highly engaged, commercially savvy solo creator with serious organic reach. She already understands marketing funnels and lead magnets from running her Squarespace/Mailchimp setup. The platform UI felt familiar and non-intimidating to her. Deal is likely to close; the main variable is her content build timeline. The institutional shelter channel (bulk licensing for shelters requiring foster parent certification) is a compelling potential expansion story. Very high-fit for the Course Creators & Digital Educators segment. Gut feel: high enthusiasm, will move when content is ready.

CALL DATE: 2026-06-25

COMPANY: Kavin Lam (company name not captured in call title)
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
Kavin Lam and Isaac Howe attended a product demo with no current LMS in place. Their company manages ~700 internal providers who need CEU courses for annual license renewals, with a planned second external tier to attract new providers. A key product gap was surfaced: Teachable does not offer a learner-facing CEU credit balance dashboard, which Kavin indicated is likely a dealbreaker.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Deliver CEU courses to internal providers and build an external marketing-tier offering to attract prospective providers
Audience: Internal providers (~700) + external/prospective providers (estimated 500+ over time)
Business model: Compliance-driven CEU delivery internally; marketing/acquisition use case externally
Content types: CEU courses; quizzes/assessments per module implied
Scale expectations: 700–1,000 to start; potentially 2,000+; uptake is uncertain

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Highly sensitive; reluctant to commit to an annual contract without knowing uptake; $6K–$13K range discussed
Authority: Kavin Lam leads evaluation; Isaac Howe involved; internal review required before any decision
Need: CEU platform with two-tier access control, learner-facing credit tracking, and flexible pricing
Timeline: Wants to move quickly; dependent on resolving pricing model and CEU tracking gap

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: None discussed
Reporting needs: Learner-facing CEU credit count vs. annual renewal requirement (gap confirmed); CSV org-level reporting
Payments / checkout: External tier may require self-enrollment checkout; not a focus in this call
Admin or seat management: Organization management for internal vs. external provider separation; CSV bulk enrollment
Special workflows or constraints: CEU credit tracking — platform cannot show users a running credit total vs. annual requirement; Kavin explicitly said the certificate-based workaround was "probably not" sufficient

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Asked Kevin to send pricing options in writing immediately
- Stated timeline as "quickly"
- Requested custom pricing for 2,000 users
- Have 700 providers ready to onboard now
- Both attendees engaged positively throughout the demo

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- CEU tracking gap: Teachable cannot provide a learner-facing credit balance dashboard showing credits earned vs. annual requirement; Kavin said the certificate workaround was "probably not" sufficient — potential dealbreaker
- Pricing sensitivity: Concerned about paying for unused seats; explicitly said "I am sensitive still to like signing a six thousand dollar contract with like four users"
- Month-to-month contract not available with full onboarding package

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Learner-facing CEU credit balance dashboard (showing running total vs. annual renewal requirement) is a top-line requirement not currently supported by Teachable

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Core (month-to-month with org management add-on); Pro ($12K–$13K/yr for up to 2K users); custom enterprise mentioned
Discounts offered: 1,000 extra users free with 2-year agreement at $12K; 1-year at $13K
Contract length discussed: Month-to-month (no onboarding) vs. annual (with onboarding, dedicated AM, SSO)
Constraints or approvals needed: Internal stakeholder review required

---

- Send Core package pricing in writing with org management add-on included
- Include Pro and 2,000-user custom quote
- Clarify month-to-month vs. annual trade-offs

Customer:
- Review pricing options internally

ATTENDEES: Jeff Baird (Transportant), Kevin Codde (Teachable), Amanda Araujo (Teachable)
COMPANY: Transportant
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Jeff Baird works at Transportant, a technology provider serving 120 school transportation districts, where he focuses on customer training and product feature adoption (current customers use ~30% of available features). He previously used Teachable at Liberty School District and reconnected after Amanda (Teachable SDR) reached out. He is evaluating two separate use cases: a Pro/Organizations plan for Transportant's B2B customer training, and a Builder plan for a personal community course on helping families dealing with addiction.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: (1) Train Transportant's 120 school district customers on the product to improve feature adoption beyond the current ~30% rate. (2) Launch a personal course for church/community members on supporting families with addiction.
Audience: School district staff (external customers of Transportant); community/church members (personal project)
Business model: Transportant includes training with product purchase or sells it separately; personal course would be sold via Teachable's seller/Builder plan
Content types: Short video + slide presentation segments for B2B; full course curriculum ready for personal project
Scale expectations: 120 organizations; 1-3 users per smaller district, 10-15 per larger; at prior employer had 200 dashboard users but only ~30 active monthly

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed explicitly; Pro plan for B2B, Builder for personal
Authority: Decisions require input from the primary platform user + CEO approval
Need: Strong for B2B — actively trying to improve customer adoption rates; existing iSpring contract in place
Timeline: iSpring renewal date unknown; Jeff will look it up

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: None specifically discussed
Reporting needs: Organization-level progress reporting and CSV export for org admins at each district
Payments / checkout: B2B training sold as standalone or bundled with product purchase; personal course sold via Teachable (Builder, 0% transaction fee)
Admin or seat management: Needs unlimited student seats per org; 15 org admin slots on Pro may be insufficient for 120 districts — Kevin noted flexibility
Special workflows or constraints: Wants maximum student enrollment per org (not seat-limited)

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Previously used Teachable at Liberty School District; retained positive impression of ease of use
- "I see a value in both organizations of using Teachable" — explicitly confirmed intent for both B2B and personal use cases
- Agreed to receive two separate written proposals
- Positive engagement throughout demo: "You guys have done a lot of work on the product"
- No pushback on platform capabilities; only question was definitional ("Is that a class?" re: 'product')

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Outbound-initiated deal (Amanda cold outreached) — lower urgency, no forcing event confirmed
- iSpring renewal date unknown — no contract timing leverage yet
- CEO approval required — Jeff is a champion but not the final decision-maker
- 15 org admin seats on Pro plan may be a constraint for managing 120 district admins

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Jeff noted that Teachable previously felt oriented around monetized/income-paying students; appreciates the newer flat-fee model
- Asked specifically about AI: wants to know who uses it in a meaningful, product-enhancing way — not just a marketing claim

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Pro plan (Transportant B2B — up to 1,000 users, 50 courses, 15 admin seats); Builder plan (personal — 0% transaction fee, up to 10 products)
Discounts offered: None mentioned
Contract length discussed: Not discussed
Constraints or approvals needed: CEO sign-off required for B2B purchase

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach: (Kevin handling)
- Send two separate proposal emails to Jeff at the same address: one for Builder plan (personal), one for Pro plan (Transportant B2B)

Customer:
- Look up iSpring contract renewal date
- Share Pro plan proposal internally with platform user and CEO

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD after internal review
- Materials to send: Written Builder and Pro package proposals

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Jeff is warm and personable — clear nostalgia for Teachable from prior use at Liberty School District. Methodical decision-maker who wants everything in writing before escalating. The World Cup in Kansas City was causing internet issues during the call. Outbound deal but genuine bi-directional interest. Two-track deal (personal + B2B) is unusual but Jeff is self-aware about the distinction and comfortable with separate plans.

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Online Course Delivery (~3:30) - "I wanted to do classes online for my work with the church and with the community. I kind of have a specialty in serving "
- Multi-format Content Upload (~4:00) - "we use video slash slide presentations for all of our customer training to support it, because our customers have... It'"
- Organizations & Multi-tenancy (~5:30) - "we have 120 school districts that use our product. So I'd be using it to train them. We're continuously coming out with "
- AI Course Generation (~7:00) - "everybody tells me that their product uses AI, but I want to know who uses it in a meaningful way that enhances the prod"
- Unlimited Student Enrollment (~9:00) - "we want as many people trained as we can because the more people in a district that knows how to use our product, the mo"
- Quiz / Assessment Builder (~11:00) - "Yes."

Budget: Not discussed

Timeline: Q4 and next year implied

Integrations: Microsoft Teams (explicitly asked)

SUMMARY
Maria Gil is the CFO of an existing Teachable customer generating $1M+ annually from online courses and high-ticket programs. The call focused on negotiating a migration from their current ThriveCart + Stripe Connect setup to Teachable Pay in exchange for a free enterprise account. She is primarily concerned about international transaction fees, long payment plan support, and exit/portability terms, and indicated she is ready to move forward pending CEO and legal approval.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Migrate payment processing from ThriveCart/Stripe Connect to Teachable Pay
Audience: Self-paced online course students; ~60% US, ~40% international (Europe, Australia, Latin America, Asia)
Business model: High-ticket course and program sales; one-time + installment payment plans; $1M+ annual revenue
Content types: Online courses and programs, including evergreen (passive) programs
Scale expectations: $1M YTD at 6 months; up to 100,000+ active students; potential for $2-3M/year

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Generating $1M+ annually; evaluating free enterprise account (Teachable Pay route) vs $10K/year plan
Authority: Maria Gil is CFO; requires CEO and legal sign-off before committing
Need: Wants better international transaction rates, unlimited students, and simplified payment processing; currently over student limits
Timeline: Decision by June 30, 2026; currently mid-program launch

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Currently using ThriveCart for checkout and Stripe Connect at 2.5% flat (US and international); Zapier integration for enrollment automation
Reporting needs: Needs full transaction and subscription data to be exportable
Payments / checkout: Requires payment plans up to 10-14 months for high-ticket offers; wants flat rate for US and international (max 3%); Stripe-based infrastructure
Admin or seat management: Needs unlimited active students and unlimited imports moving forward
Special workflows or constraints: Offers lifetime access to programs; existing students have lifetime access commitments; concerned about account terms if revenue fluctuates

---

- Already calculated revenue impact at different transaction fee rates ($1M/year flow; compared 2.5% vs 3%)
- Came in with prepared list of questions; methodical due diligence suggests serious intent

---

- International transaction fees: Teachable's standard 3.9% international rate is higher than their current 2.5% flat; explicitly asked for ~3% flat on all transactions
- Revenue fluctuation concern: Worried free account could be lost if annual volume dips to $300K in a slow year (evergreen-only)
- CEO/legal approval required before finalizing
- Mid-program launch limits available time for evaluation and migration

---

- Found "active student" vs "import" terminology confusing — required clarification
- Would benefit from clearer documentation on what changes operationally when migrating from ThriveCart to Teachable Pay

---

Plan discussed: Free enterprise account (conditional on Teachable Pay) vs $10K/year plan (100K students, 20K imports)
Discounts offered: Kevin offered to negotiate international transaction rate; confirmed overage fee waiver under both options
Contract length discussed: 1-year Teachable Pay commitment; auto-renewable
Constraints or approvals needed: CEO and legal team approval; wants all terms in writing before committing

---

Kevin:
- Send written agreement summary with confirmed transaction rates (US and international)
- Confirm international fee can be negotiated to ~3% flat
- Confirm free account is preserved if annual volume stays above $300K
- Confirm long payment plan support (10-14 months) in Teachable Pay

STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
TheraMoves Services is a continuing education provider for therapists (OTs, PTs, SLPs) and special educators with 18 on-demand video courses currently spread across GoToWebinar and Zoom. They want to consolidate onto a single platform supporting per-user access expiration, completion tracking, automated certificate delivery, and PDF/link integration within courses. They evaluated the Growth plan positively ($139/mo annual) and are ready to start a 7-day trial.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Consolidate 18 on-demand CE courses from GoToWebinar and Zoom onto one unified platform
Audience: Occupational therapists, speech therapists, physical therapists, and special educators completing continuing education requirements
Business model: B2C course sales via theramoves.com; current payment via Stripe/WordPress; considering eventual migration to Teachable checkout
Content types: Pre-recorded video courses (2–11 hours), single-module format, post-course quizzes (currently via Google Forms), per-course PDFs and CE compliance forms
Scale expectations: ~15–20 concurrent learners; 18 courses now, targeting 24–25 within a year; solo admin

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Growth at $139/mo annual accepted unprompted
Authority: Owner/admin on call alongside business partner Malkie K; financial partner not clearly identified on call; developer needed for website/Zapier integration
Need: Clearly established — GoToWebinar lacks playback speed control and hit file size limits; Mailchimp unsubscribe issue causes students to lose access to course links
Timeline: No hard deadline; wants to start with 3 courses on 7-day trial, then migrate all 18 gradually

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Stripe (current payment processor), Mailchimp (email marketing), Zapier (for Stripe-to-Teachable automated enrollment automation)
Reporting needs: Time-on-course tracking, video completion stats
Payments / checkout: Currently Stripe via WordPress; considering Teachable Pay long-term; QuickBooks integration a concern for financial partner
Admin or seat management: Solo admin
Special workflows or constraints: Per-user access expiration starting from enrollment date (not fixed course-wide date); existing quizzes in Google Forms — does not want to rebuild 18 courses in Teachable quiz format; automated enrollment via Stripe/Zapier required (manual student entry is a deal-breaker); developer needed for website redirect to Teachable

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "The 139 price for the year I think would be just fine" — price accepted unprompted
- "It really sounds really good" — strong positive reaction after certificate feature demo

---

- Website sensitivity: "Our website is extremely sensitive... Anytime we make a change to it, we get so many problems"
- Zapier skepticism: "I once tried to use [Zapier]. It didn't work"
- Financial partner not on call; QuickBooks dependency may complicate Teachable Pay adoption
- Near deal-breaker moment when manual student enrollment was discovered — resolved once Stripe/Zapier path was explained
- Reluctant to rebuild 18 courses' worth of quizzes in Teachable format: "There's no way I'm doing that"
- Migration seen as daunting: "That'll be really nightmarish"

---

- Video playback speed control is a key differentiator — GoToWebinar lacking it directly drove dissatisfaction
- Course pages need tabbed layout (description, learning outcomes, agenda, CEU details) — single-page layout in Teachable demo felt insufficient for their course structure
- Per-user access expiration must auto-calculate from enrollment date, not be set as a course-wide fixed date

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth ($139/mo annual, $189/mo monthly)
Discounts offered: None
Contract length discussed: Annual preferred
Constraints or approvals needed: Financial partner manages payments; developer needed for Stripe/Zapier technical integration

---

- Send Growth plan details and trial sign-up link via email
- Send help guide / getting-started video links

Customer:
- Start 7-day free trial with 3 courses
- Contact developer to assess Stripe-Teachable Zapier integration feasibility

calls.title: Connect with Teachable - Zach / Dave
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-24
ATTENDEES: Jameson (unknown), Dave Baldwin (unknown)
COMPANY: Corvita
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Corvita is a menopausal care organization selling CE-accredited courses to healthcare providers (med spa owners, aesthetic practitioners). Jameson and Dave are consultants contracted by Corvita to evaluate and select an LMS. They received a full platform demo and are actively comparing options with a decision deadline of ~2 weeks.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Sell continuing-education-accredited menopausal care training courses to healthcare providers via both B2C (individual purchases) and B2B (organizations/centers purchasing seat-based access as part of a wider service offering).
Audience: Med spa owners, aesthetic practitioners, other menopausal care providers
Business model: B2B + B2C course sales; B2B involves bundling course access into a service package sold to individual practices/centers
Content types: Text, images, video (currently stored in EasyGenerator)
Scale expectations: Multiple courses across pre- and peri-menopause topics; managing multiple B2B client organizations with per-center admin portals

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not explicitly stated; aware of $7K/yr base plan and $12K enterprise tier
Authority: Jameson and Dave are contractors advising; final decision rests with the Corvita founder/team
Need: High — actively migrating off EasyGenerator, need to start selling ASAP
Timeline: Decision in ~2 weeks; large marketing planning meeting in ~1 month

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: HubSpot CRM (via webhooks/Zapier for self-enrollment capture); Stripe payment processing; future API usage possible
Reporting needs: Org-level reporting so center managers can track staff completion without manual reports; CE/accreditation completion tracking
Payments / checkout: Teachable native Stripe processing preferred (greenfield); membership/subscription billing for ongoing org access; future-proofing for Stripe data portability if they build custom LMS
Admin or seat management: Organizations feature for per-center B2B clients; center-level admin reporting portals
Special workflows or constraints: CE accreditation requirements; enforced video scrub prevention for compliance; need content portability/data ownership confirmed for future exit strategy

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Jameson said "As soon as possible" when asked about timeline
- Dave acknowledged pricing is "a little bit more" than alternatives but immediately followed with recognizing the value: "there's a huge amount of flexibility and functionality here that we didn't know"

SUMMARY
JanHenrik Storgards is a long-term Teachable customer (since 2019) running a video games creation course platform tied to the Finnish university system, with ~92,000 enrolled students and 72,000 active email subscribers. The call was triggered by an upcoming pricing change that would increase his costs from ~$2,800/year to ~$4,500/month, prompting him to consider switching platforms. Kevin presented three more affordable pricing options and JanHenrik ended the call open to staying pending team review.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Host and deliver video game creation courses to Finnish and international learners
Audience: Finnish citizens (free tier) and international students (monthly/yearly subscription)
Business model: Freemium for Finnish users; subscription (~$9.90/month or yearly) for international students
Content types: Video content (200+ hours), some assessment tools (using SurveyMonkey externally)
Scale expectations: 92,000 enrolled; growing by 10-20 students/day; 72,000 active email subscribers

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: $2,800/year was acceptable; $4,500/month is not; open to ~$6,600/year (150K students) or ~$5,400/year (50K students)
Authority: Has significant decision-making authority but must consult team and a Finnish university stakeholder
Need: Urgent — pricing renewal in November; actively considering switching platforms
Timeline: November renewal; a few months to decide

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Fast Spring (current payment processor), Google Analytics (traffic monitoring), custom-built student dashboard connected to Teachable accounts
Reporting needs: Real-time active user monitoring, completion tracking, usage statistics
Payments / checkout: European payment methods (PayPal unavailable in many EU countries); VAT-inclusive gross pricing display (legally required in EU/UK); multi-country VAT compliance across 35-40 countries; currently using Fast Spring which handles these requirements
Admin or seat management: Bulk unenroll ~20,000 inactive students to manage active user count
Special workflows or constraints: Free tier for Finnish citizens; paid international tiers with monthly and annual plans; uses Fast Spring for payment processing outside Teachable

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Expressed relief and said "I feel more calm" after hearing revised pricing options
- Switching platforms described as a "massive change" — 200+ hours of hosted video content creates high switching cost
- Has been a Teachable customer 5+ years and was interviewed as a success story a year ago
- Open to migrating back to Teachable Pay if payment methods and rates are competitive
- Said "it's good that we are talking now"

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Strongly considering switching; already evaluating alternative platforms
- Long history of unresolved customer support issues — team is "annoyed"; service described as "really bad" consistently over 5 years
- Currently happy with Fast Spring's responsiveness and European payment coverage
- EU/UK VAT compliance concern: Teachable displays net prices but EU/UK law requires gross (VAT-inclusive) pricing — potentially non-compliant for their European student base
- Historical double billing issue damaged trust even though it is now resolved
- Decision requires buy-in from team and possibly a Finnish university stakeholder

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Admin dashboard lacks real-time user activity; had to integrate Google Analytics separately for traffic monitoring
- Student learner dashboard was so poor they built a custom one on top of Teachable accounts
- Quizzes didn't work for their use case — now using SurveyMonkey externally for assessments
- Completion tracking does not work reliably for their needs
- Customer support rated very poor; issues reported over years without resolution
- Double billing during payment setup caused significant customer complaints
- Positive: Video hosting service and content upload praised strongly
- Positive: Learner UX once inside the course described as "quite good"
- Positive: Translation/multi-language support noted as working well

Plan discussed: Advanced plan; three options presented by Kevin: (1) 150K students @ $6,600/year ($550/mo), (2) 50K students @ $5,400/year ($450/mo), (3) Unlimited via Teachable Pay (rate TBD based on Fast Spring comparison)
Discounts offered: Overage fees waived as part of new plan
Contract length discussed: November renewal referenced; no explicit multi-year discussion
Constraints or approvals needed: Team approval and possible university stakeholder sign-off required

---

- Send email with all three pricing options in writing
- Include bulk unenroll instructions for inactive students
- Research competitive transaction rates vs. Fast Spring; provide Teachable Pay fee structure
- Provide list of supported European payment methods
- Potentially include dedicated support manager option with add-on pricing

Customer (JanHenrik):
- Share Fast Spring transaction rates for Kevin's team to compare
- Review written proposals with team
- Consult with Finnish university stakeholder
- Respond with preferred direction before November renewal

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD — possible follow-up call after email exchange
- Materials to send: Written pricing proposals, payment method list, bulk unenroll instructions

---

JanHenrik is assertive, business-savvy, and direct — explicitly called out that investor buyout drove price increases. He is genuinely proud of their product ("the Netflix of video games craziness") and has stayed with Teachable through years of issues largely due to inertia and the strength of video hosting. CALL DATE: 2026-06-22
ATTENDEES: IFPO Admin (email unknown), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: IFPO
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
IFPO is a professional training and certification organization currently locked into a 20-year-old LMS run by Smart Horizons that they cannot update independently. They sell training programs B2B to 75+ corporate organizations and also directly to individual buyers globally. They are actively evaluating Teachable (plus 2-3 other platforms this week) with a hard deadline to go live by September for a major trade show.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Replace Smart Horizons LMS and bring course content management in house
Audience: Corporate organizations (75+ client orgs, each with employees) and individual direct buyers; global reach
Business model: B2B seat-based training sales to companies + direct individual purchases via website (WooCommerce shop)
Content types: Video courses, PDFs, ebooks (currently on Amazon Kindle), digital downloads, live webinars (Zoom), quizzes/exams
Scale expectations: Typically under 1,000 active users at a time; largest single client has ~450 employees; phased rollout starting with one smaller flagship course

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: $12,000/year (Pro plan discussed); favorably received vs. competitors quoting $47-50k
Authority: IFPO Admin drives evaluation and has input, but CEO makes final call; currently narrowing down platforms
Need: Very high — current platform is 20+ years old, they cannot update content independently, enrollment takes 2-3 days manually
Timeline: Goal to be live with at least one course by September trade show; open to phased rollout

---
TECHNAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Credly (digital credential badges via API after course completion), Zoom (live webinars), WooCommerce (existing shop); third-party proctoring tool needed
Reporting needs: Admin reporting by course/date range; organization-level reporting; export capability
Payments / checkout: Stripe; one-time purchase and subscription options; automated enrollment upon purchase (critical — currently 2-3 day manual delay)
Admin or seat management: Organizations feature critical — 75+ client orgs each with employee groups; org-level admin roles needed
Special workflows or constraints: Proctored/monitored exams required (browser lockdown capability); content update control must be in-house; global delivery; ebook with watermarking/DRM question unresolved; may import SCORM-packaged courses from external developers

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "I really like this a lot" after full platform demo
- Favorably comparing Teachable pricing to competitors ($47-50k quoted elsewhere); called it a "good price point"
- Requested free trial link to explore independently
- Hard deadline: September trade show as go-live target
- Positive UI reaction: "I like the outface. It looks good. Some of them don't look very good."
- Asked Kevin to send pricing in writing to share with CEO — champion building internal buy-in

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Teachable cannot provide browser lockdown proctoring; prospect says they have a workaround but it is a gap
- CEO approval required before commitment
- Credly digital badge integration requires API/developer work, not out-of-the-box
- Evaluating at least 2-3 other platforms this same week
- Ebook watermarking question unanswered — Kevin to follow up

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Prospect asked whether Teachable adds watermarks to purchased ebook downloads — Kevin did not know, needs follow-up
- Certificates limited to downloadable PDFs only; prospect currently uses Credly for digital badge credentials via email
- Browser lockdown proctoring not available in platform

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Pro plan at $12,000/year (up to 1,000 active users)
Discounts offered: None mentioned
Contract length discussed: Annual
Constraints or approvals needed: CEO sign-off required; admin is narrowing options before presenting

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send pricing summary and collateral in writing for prospect to share with CEO
- Provide free trial/sandbox link
- Follow up on ebook watermarking question

Customer:
- Complete remaining platform evaluations (2-3 more meetings this week)
- Share Teachable info with CEO
- Explore free trial

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD after CEO review
- Materials to send: Pricing sheet, free trial link, ebook watermark follow-up answer

CALL DATE: 2026-06-22
ATTENDEES: Annie Zempel (Greylock Academy), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Greylock Academy
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Greylock Academy is the customer training arm of a security observability platform company, currently on LearnWorlds with SCORM content plus a separate lab platform (Instruct) for live security analyst training. Annie Zempel, who owns the academy, joined this initial discovery/demo call to evaluate Teachable as she looks to expand self-paced on-demand training. She is not the final decision-maker — the unnamed program director runs day-to-day operations and would be the primary evaluator.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Expand on-demand, self-paced training for external customer security analysts, complementing existing live webinar training
Audience: External customers (security analysts across healthcare, banking, education sectors)
Business model: Mix of paid and free customer training; onboarding-focused when new customers are activated
Content types: SCORM/video modules + live Zoom webinars + hands-on labs (hosted separately in Instruct)
Scale expectations: ~100–200 students/month (mix of net new and returning)

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Pro plan at $12K/year was discussed; no commitment or budget confirmation
Authority: Annie owns the academy org but is not the program decision-maker; deferred to program director for evaluation
Need: Moderate — pain is lack of integration between LMS and lab platform; evaluating before November LearnWorlds renewal
Timeline: Will spend summer in discovery; decision expected by end of year with renewal in November

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: FusionAuth for SSO (explicit hard requirement); HubSpot for account management; open API needed to connect with lab platform (Instruct)
Reporting needs: Analytics on new student onboarding per month/quarter; org-admin access for team leads
Payments / checkout: Some content is paid, some free; payment collection via Teachable is optional
Admin or seat management: Per-organization course assignment; up to ~1,000 active users anticipated; org-level admins for reporting
Special workflows or constraints: Two-platform friction (LMS + lab) is their primary pain — API integration between Teachable and Instruct is the critical differentiator

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Explicitly asked about SSO support, connecting to existing FusionAuth setup
- Asked proactively about open API as a possible integration path
- Proactively asked to move to pricing discussion
- Offered to share proposal with program director and facilitate follow-up

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Annie's candid initial impression: "it's not offering us much more granularity than we have with Learn Worlds today"
- Annie is not the buyer — program director not present and must be engaged separately
- Long timeline (5+ months to decision); renewal pressure in November
- Training is heavily lab-centric; LMS is secondary — Teachable alone doesn't solve their core integration pain

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Annie found the platform "pretty standard" relative to LearnWorlds; no standout differentiation in this demo
- Core frustration with LearnWorlds is lack of lab integration — this is the problem to solve, not LMS features

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Pro plan — SSO, 1,000 active users, 50 courses, dedicated account manager, onboarding support; $12,000/year
Discounts offered: None discussed
Contract length discussed: Annual implied
Constraints or approvals needed: Program director approval required

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Send written pricing/features summary for Annie to forward to program director

Customer:
- Annie to share materials with program director
- Program director to follow up if interested

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Not scheduled; awaiting program director engagement
- Materials to send: Written proposal/pricing summary

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Annie is knowledgeable and pragmatic — she asked all the right technical questions (SSO, API, branding per org, seat counting) but was candid that Teachable doesn't stand out above LearnWorlds from what she saw. The real opportunity is in demonstrating the API/integration story to the program director. Medium-low deal probability until the program director is engaged.

CALL DATE: 2026-06-19
ATTENDEES: Ajay Menendez, Zach McCall (Teachable), Giovana Carvalho (Teachable)
COMPANY: Ajay Menendez (Independent Cybersecurity Educator)
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Ajay Menendez is an independent cybersecurity educator with 10+ years of experience training Fortune 100 companies and DoD clients, planning to build an online asynchronous cybersecurity academy on Teachable. He has a clear vision — subscription pricing ($50/month), à la carte coaching, and a B2B in-person training track — but is not ready to purchase until content is built. His stated timeline is Fall 2027, though Giovana pitched an earlier entry using the upcoming book launch as a catalyst.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Build an online asynchronous cybersecurity academy covering 500-600 hours of video, labs, and walkthroughs for beginners and career-changers
Audience: Career-changers, new graduates entering cybersecurity (consumer); Fortune 100 companies and DoD clients (B2B in-person)
Business model: Subscription ($50/month), à la carte coaching hours (pay-per-session); separate B2B contracts for week-long in-person training
Content types: Video-heavy, labs/walkthroughs, PDFs, knowledge checks; live coaching sessions
Scale expectations: Volume-focused global audience; 500-600 hours of content across multiple modules with structured prerequisites

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed
Authority: Sole decision-maker; independent creator
Need: High — clear vision, pedagogy, and pricing model established
Timeline: Follow-up August 5, 2026 (11am ET); purchase decision Fall 2027

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Zoom or other video tool for live coaching/synchronous sessions
Reporting needs: Per-student progress tracking; B2B organization reporting for corporate clients
Payments / checkout: Subscription billing ($50/mo), à la carte coaching purchases, bundle options
Admin or seat management: Organization management for B2B clients (Boeing, Lockheed Martin, etc.)

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-18
ATTENDEES: Josh Adkins, Karen Ward, Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Josh Adkins (Real Estate, NC)
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
Josh Adkins and Karen Ward from a North Carolina real estate office (referred via a Keller Williams coaching connection in Portland, ME) attended a product demo with Kevin Codde. They manage approximately 200 real estate agents who need compliance and onboarding training tied to North Carolina Real Estate Commission (NCREC) requirements. They are evaluating Teachable to deliver self-paced online courses for dual-career agents who cannot attend in-person training, with quiz-based completion verification to satisfy regulatory obligations.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Train new real estate agents on compliance, forms, and NCREC-mandated requirements
Audience: ~200 real estate agents (internal workforce), including dual-career agents with limited daytime availability
Business model: Internal training — not selling courses externally
Content types: YouTube videos, quizzes, forms/PDF materials, compliance courses
Scale expectations: ~200 active agents; variable monthly new agent enrollment (2–10/month)

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: $4,800/year discussed (LMS Core, discounted from $6,000/year list)
Authority: Josh and Karen are evaluators; require sign-off from other team members before committing
Need: High — NCREC regulatory compliance driving a genuine training requirement
Timeline: No fixed go-live date; evaluating to find the right platform

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: YouTube video content for courses; SSO with active directory mentioned by rep (prospect did not confirm this as a stated need)
Reporting needs: Track that agents completed required compliance courses
Payments / checkout: N/A — internal training, not selling courses
Admin or seat management: Up to 5 admin users; ~250 active student slots; monthly rolling enrollment of new agents
Special workflows or constraints: Monthly new agent onboarding with variable batch sizes; NCREC compliance verification requirement

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Engaged actively throughout the demo with use-case-specific questions
- Josh asked about AI quiz generation from YouTube videos — actively probing for workflow fit
- Karen proactively suggested bundling courses as a workflow solution, showing platform comprehension and implementation thinking
- Requested a written pricing proposal to take to leadership for approval

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Need team consensus and leadership approval before committing
- Price sensitivity: Karen asked for enterprise features at growth plan pricing
- Josh is skeptical of White Glove service value based on a past experience where onboarding was underwhelming — Kevin should set clear expectations in the written proposal
- No fixed go-live date; evaluation timeline is open-ended

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Karen: "it seems very user friendly" (positive reaction to course creation UX)
- Josh was confused by the "$2 per user" pricing display — interpreted it as an additive per-user fee on top of the package price; Kevin clarified it represents the per-user average at 250 seats, not an additional charge

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: LMS Core (enterprise package)
Discounts offered: Referral discount — $500/month dropped to $400/month ($4,800/year vs $6,000/year list)
Contract length discussed: Annual; monthly payment option available
Constraints or approvals needed: Josh and Karen must present to other team members for final approval

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin Codde:
- Send written pricing proposal for the $4,800/year LMS Core package with plan comparison

Customer:
- Review proposal internally with other team members
- Present pricing to leadership for approval

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD (pending internal team review)
- Materials to send: Written pricing summary and plan comparison

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Referred via a Keller Williams coaching network (coach in Portland, ME). Josh runs point on the evaluation; Karen is a co-evaluator with an operational/administrative orientation. Josh's tone was direct and pragmatic; he questioned White Glove service credibility based on past disappointments — the proposal should clearly outline deliverables. The deal is driven by a genuine regulatory need (NCREC compliance), which creates real urgency even without a hard go-live date. Seriousness level: medium-high.

- Compliance Controls (~8:30) - "They gotta do like a compliance class or course or a forms class... from a compliance side and the North Carolina Real E"

- Completion Tracking (~16:30) - "to make sure from a compliance side and the North Carolina Real Estate Commission side that we're making sure our agents"
- Group Enrollment (~8:00) - "every month we're gonna have new agents. So it could be two agents one month, five agents the next, seven the next one, "

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-18
ATTENDEES: Darja Galante (VEON), Hassan Tariq (VEON), Compliance TrainingsVEON (VEON), Amanda Araujo (Teachable), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: VEON
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
VEON is a large multinational telecom company (Dubai HQ, operations across Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and South Asia; ~15-16K employees) with an internal ethics and compliance team looking to modernize their compliance training LMS. They are currently using TR Alliant and are unhappy with content quality and platform flexibility, with ~1.5-2 years remaining on that contract. They want a platform to deliver ethics/compliance training (anti-bribery, anti-corruption, sanctions, gifts & hospitality) to internal HQ employees (~100-120 initially) and eventually to external third-party vendors/suppliers (up to 20-30K), and plan to start a parallel rollout now for non-mandatory and third-party training.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Supplement current LMS now and fully replace TR Alliant after contract expiry; deliver ethics and compliance training to employees and supply chain partners.
Audience: Internal HQ employees (~100-120 initially, growing to 15-16K org-wide) + external third-party vendors/suppliers (potentially 20-30K)
Business model: Corporate compliance training program — mandatory training for employees and third parties
Content types: SCORM-packaged video content with embedded quizzes; custom-authored ethics/compliance curriculum
Scale expectations: Start with ~100 HQ users; scale to full org (15-16K) and up to 30K third parties

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not formally defined. Preference for lump-sum or bulk pricing for large volumes. Rejected LinkedIn Learning for being too expensive and inflexible (min 4,400-user packages). Kevin indicated Teachable would be "under $100K" for their use case.
Authority: Darja Galante is the project lead driving this evaluation. "Saeed" was expected on the call but absent — may be a peer or approver.
Need: High — actively evaluating alternatives, frustrated with current LMS, specific requirements around SCORM, multi-language, TPRM system integration, and user segmentation between internal/external.
Timeline: Would start small parallel rollout immediately for non-mandatory/third-party training; full migration post-contract expiry (~1.5-2 years).

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Third-party risk management (TPRM) system (to auto-assign training to vendors), SCORM format support
Reporting needs: Completion/certification tracking (especially for external third parties as compliance evidence)
Payments / checkout: Not discussed
Admin or seat management: Must segment internal employees vs. external third-party vendors; limited/temporary access licenses for vendor training
Special workflows or constraints: Multilingual content required (Ukrainian, Russian mandatory; English + local languages for Pakistan, Bangladesh, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan)

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Clear dissatisfaction with current LMS (TR Alliant) on both content quality and platform flexibility
- Willing to start a parallel deployment now even while locked into existing contract
- Very large user volume potential (15-16K employees + up to 30K third parties) — significant deal size
- All prospect attendees engaged positively and agreed to schedule a full demo
- Explicitly asked about outsourcing content design/animation to a service provider

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Locked into TR Alliant contract for ~1.5-2 years — full migration timeline is delayed
- Budget not formally defined; pricing sensitivity given large target user volumes
- TPRM system integration requirement needs technical validation
- "Saeed" was absent — possible additional stakeholder or approver whose buy-in is needed
- Content authoring/design services request may exceed standard Teachable offering

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Wants SCORM-compatible LMS with better content authoring/customization tools than current provider
- Interested in templated or partially-built compliance content they can customize with their own scripts
- Needs robust multilingual support for Eastern European and Central/South Asian languages
- Prefers lump-sum or volume-based pricing over per-user pricing for large deployments

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Not specified; Kevin mentioned Teachable would be "under $100K" for their scale
Discounts offered: None discussed
Contract length discussed: Not discussed
Constraints or approvals needed: Budget not yet formally defined; approval process unclear

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- N/A (not on call)

Customer:
- Confirm availability for full platform demo with Kevin

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Demo to be scheduled (Amanda coordinating post-call)
- Materials to send: None mentioned

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Darja Galante is well-organized and provided comprehensive context upfront — clearly has done her homework on what they need. Team spans Dubai, Pakistan, and other geographies. Previously used TRACE (before current vendor), now on TR Alliant; also evaluated LinkedIn Learning (rejected for inflexible packaging and pricing). Kevin was confident this is a good fit and enthusiastically invited them to a demo. High-volume deal potential with significant long-term upside. Key risk is the 1.5-2 year contract lock-in and the absent stakeholder "Saeed." Gut feel: serious prospect with real need, strong potential for a meaningful deal — timeline will be phased.

---

- Multi-language Support (~6:52) - "So we have Ukrainian, Russian languages that we definitely need to cover."
- SCORM Support (~8:46) - "for now we are using that SCORM format. If there is another way how this can be done, we are definitely open to that."

- Organization Hierarchy / Nesting (~13:44) - "I think we should distinguish here...between training for internal employees...And the training for the third parties yo"
- Access Duration / Expiration (~13:20) - "we may be required the limited licenses because we will not be giving them the permanent license."

CALL DATE: 2026-06-18
ATTENDEES: Darja Galante (VEON), Hassan Tariq (VEON), Abdul (VEON)
COMPANY: VEON
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
VEON is a Dubai-headquartered telecom company with ~15,000+ employees running a mandatory ethics and compliance program covering anti-bribery, anti-corruption, sanctions, and ESG topics. They are evaluating LMS platforms to replace their current provider Triant, though they are locked into that contract for ~1.5-2 more years and plan to begin a parallel rollout of non-mandatory training and third-party compliance training now.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Deliver mandatory compliance and ethics training to internal employees and external third-party suppliers/vendors/JV partners
Audience: ~100-120 Dubai HQ employees initially, scaling to all operating units (15,000-16,000 total employees); up to 20,000-30,000 third-party vendors/suppliers at full scale
Business model: Internal compliance program (not a commercial training business)
Content types: Video-based compliance training (anti-bribery, anti-corruption, sanctions, gifts/hospitality, ESG, leadership/conduct); currently packaged as SCORM; wants interactive quizzes embedded
Scale expectations: Start small (~100 users at HQ), full rollout across decentralized operating units in UAE, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ukraine, Russia, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Undefined; early shopping phase; prefers lump-sum/flat-rate pricing for large volumes; strongly price-sensitive — rejected LinkedIn Learning as too expensive and inflexible
Authority: Darja Galante leads the evaluation (ethics & compliance team); Abdul, Hassan, and Nisar are team members; additional stakeholder "Saeed" was invited but did not join
Need: High — unhappy with Triant content quality; creating all content in-house and just packaging it as SCORM
Timeline: Can begin non-mandatory and third-party training now in parallel with Triant; full migration in ~1.5-2 years when contract expires

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Must connect to their third-party risk management system for automated training assignment to vendors/suppliers
Reporting needs: Completion tracking and certificate issuance required for compliance audit purposes
Payments / checkout: N/A — internal compliance deployment, not commercial
Admin or seat management: Need to distinguish internal employee learners from external third-party learners; third parties need limited-term (non-permanent) licenses; users archived after completion
Special workflows or constraints: Multi-language content required — Ukrainian and Russian are definite; English covers Pakistan, Bangladesh, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan with local language preferred where feasible

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Provided detailed, unprompted use case overview on first discovery call
- Requested sandbox/test login to explore the platform hands-on before or after the demo
- Committed to scheduling demo for Monday (week of 2026-06-22)

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Locked into Triant contract for ~1.5-2 years; full migration is deferred
- Strong price sensitivity; wants affordable/flat-rate pricing; rejected LinkedIn Learning as too expensive
- Large potential third-party learner volume (20,000-30,000) may require custom enterprise pricing
- Multiple stakeholders spread across geographies; time-zone complexity (Dubai/Pakistan/California)

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Want tools to design/animate compliance content and embed quizzes (willing to create content themselves but need polished production capabilities)
- Open to moving away from SCORM if Teachable offers a better/equivalent workflow
- Prefer lump-sum pricing over per-user at large volumes

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: No specific plan; Kevin mentioned "under $100K easily" as a general range
Discounts offered: None
Contract length discussed: Not discussed
Constraints or approvals needed: Budget not yet defined; early shopping phase

ATTENDEES: Mikhail Barannikov (email unknown), Kevin Codde (Teachable)

STAGE: Followup

---
SUMMARY
Mikhail is an existing Teachable customer on a 2-year contract. He reached out to clarify whether student limits apply to his plan after the AI support chatbot gave him confusing information. Kevin confirmed his current plan locks in unlimited students for the duration of the contract.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Confirm no student count limits during active 2-year contract
Audience: External students (non-paying; Mikhail pays Teachable on their behalf)
Business model: Free or subsidized course delivery at scale
Scale expectations: Potentially 10,000+ students

---
QUALIFICATION
Need: Contract term clarity on student limits
Timeline: Active — approximately 9 months into a 2-year contract

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Concerned that student limits were retroactively introduced after he signed an unlimited contract
- Mentioned potential cancellation and prorated refund if limits were enforced
- AI support chatbot gave misleading or overwhelming information about contract terms, causing unnecessary alarm

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- AI support chatbot provided confusing or excessive information that led to misunderstanding of contract terms
- Customer requested a short written confirmation of terms (2 sentences max)

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send brief written confirmation email: no student limits until end of 2-year contract; new terms apply at renewal

Customer:
- Awaiting confirmation email

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: None scheduled
- Materials to send: Written confirmation of unlimited student terms through contract end

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Mikhail is pragmatic and low-maintenance — just wants written assurance and no further contact for two years. He explicitly referenced Kajabi and Podia as having student limits, and chose Teachable originally because it did not. Risk of downstream churn if the AI support chatbot continues to give existing customers unclear contract information.

CALL DATE: 2026-06-17
ATTENDEES: Michael Myers (no email captured), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Michael Myers International Ministry
STAGE: Demo

---
SUMMARY
Michael Myers leads an international Christian ministry based in Ohio/Indiana with 21 active schools in the Philippines and permission to scale to 2,000 schools. He came to the call primarily to ask about nonprofit pricing and to see a demo. He is evaluating Teachable as a plug-and-play training solution for volunteers who are then deployed to teach students in the Philippines.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Train volunteers online using a standardized curriculum so they can teach at Philippine schools without requiring annual in-person training from Michael.
Audience: Ministry volunteers (train-the-trainer model); currently 21 schools, potential 2,000+.
Business model: Non-profit ministry. Not selling courses. Pending a grant expected in December 2026.
Content types: Video, PDFs, quizzes, certificates; follows an 11-chapter curriculum book.
Scale expectations: Small batches initially (50-250 volunteers at a time), but significant long-term scale.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Uncertain. Core plan at ~$450/month may be cost-prohibitive; dependent on a December 2026 grant. Prospect is a developer and may self-build if cost is prohibitive.
Authority: Appears to be the founder and decision-maker of the ministry.
Need: Real need — can only visit Philippines annually; volunteers need asynchronous training they can complete independently.
Timeline: Grant expected December 2026; no hard deadline otherwise.

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Not discussed.
Reporting needs: Not discussed in detail.
Payments / checkout: Non-profit; not selling courses. Needs nonprofit pricing.
Admin or seat management: Small admin team. Train-the-trainer model.
Special workflows or constraints: 12-hour time zone difference; asynchronous completion required. Critical barrier: Philippines volunteers primarily use Facebook, not email — but Teachable requires email for login.

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Actively engaged with demo and asked specific questions about quiz mechanics, certificate automation, and video enforcement
- Confirmed interest in the free trial
- Framed evaluation as plug-and-play vs. self-building — cost is the deciding factor

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Price is #1 concern — $450/month is likely cost-prohibitive pending grant
- Prospect is a developer who may self-build if too expensive
- Email-required login is a significant barrier for Philippines volunteers who primarily use Facebook
- No budget set aside; dependent on December 2026 grant outcome

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Nonprofit pricing is not visible on the Teachable website — caused friction in getting to the right person (had to go through Amanda then schedule with Kevin)
- Email-required login is a real blocker for the Philippines volunteer use case

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Core ($500/month → ~$450 with 10% nonprofit discount); Growth plan also shown
Discounts offered: 10% nonprofit discount
Contract length discussed: Annual commitment with monthly or annual billing option
Constraints or approvals needed: Waiting on grant (December 2026)

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Send follow-up email with free trial link and pricing page (teachable.com/pricing)

Customer:
- Explore free trial
- Await grant decision (December 2026)
- Evaluate cost vs. self-building

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD — prospect will follow up once grant decision is known
- Materials to send: Pricing page link, free trial signup

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Michael is a pastor and ministry founder — very direct communicator who cut straight to pricing at the start of the call. Has technical chops (developer background) so has a credible self-build alternative. The Philippines email constraint is a genuine platform limitation for this use case. Seriousness level: Medium — real need and genuine engagement with the demo, but cost and the email login barrier are real hurdles. Earliest realistic timeline is Q4 2026 pending grant.

CALL DATE: 2026-06-17
ATTENDEES: Darla Zarley (email not provided), Kevin Codde (Teachable - internal)
COMPANY: Nevada State Agency
STAGE: Followup

---
SUMMARY
Darla Zarley manages Teachable for a Nevada state government agency that uses it exclusively for a mandatory licensee law quiz required every two years. The call was triggered by an overage flag showing ~18,500 active users on a 5,000-seat Growth plan. During the call, Darla bulk-unenrolled all users from all courses, inadvertently causing all completion certificates to disappear — a critical compliance issue since Nevada law requires the agency to maintain proof of licensure completion for audits.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Mandatory compliance training — licensees must complete a law quiz every two years to maintain their state license
Audience: State licensees (~18,500 historical, ~5,000 active at any given time)
Business model: Free to licensees; they pay for the license itself, not the course; agency is government-funded
Content types: Law quiz (recertification course rebuilt every 2 years; old courses unpublished, only current one live)
Scale expectations: ~5,000 active licensees at any time; must retain historical records for 18,500+

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Needs boss approval for any additional spending; renewal was June 18th (next day)
Authority: Darla manages the platform but cannot approve upgrades unilaterally
Need: CRITICAL — must restore deleted completion certificates for regulatory compliance; ongoing need to manage user counts without losing compliance history
Timeline: Account renewal June 18th; support escalation ongoing

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: None mentioned
Reporting needs: Year-by-year view of quiz completions; ability to audit individual licensee accounts for certificate of completion
Payments / checkout: None (free to learners)
Admin or seat management: Needs to manage 18,500+ historical users without losing certificate/completion history; currently ~3.7x over Growth plan active user limit
Special workflows or constraints: Must maintain completion certificates per Nevada law; agency auditors randomly select 500 licensees and verify certificate existence in individual accounts

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Engaged with Advanced plan pricing ($309/month, $3,708/year) when prompted
- Account renewal next day — high urgency
- Proactively logged into Teachable admin during call to take action

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- CRITICAL DATA LOSS: Darla bulk-unenrolled all 18,500+ users from all courses, causing all completion certificates to disappear. This is a Nevada legal compliance risk.
- Needs boss approval for any plan upgrade — decision not unilateral
- Confused about what counts as an "active user" vs. historical/stored user; the platform's definition doesn't match her mental model of "active"

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Bulk unenrollment removes certificate visibility — customers expect historical certificates to persist even when students are unenrolled from a course
- No easy way to archive or export historical compliance records at the user level before taking bulk actions
- No visible backup or undo functionality for bulk admin operations
- "Active user" definition is confusing for government use cases where learners complete once and are rarely active again

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Advanced plan — 10,000 active students, $309/month, $3,708/year
Discounts offered: None
Contract length discussed: Annual (renewal June 18th)
Constraints or approvals needed: Boss approval required for any upgrade

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- (Kevin's account) Ensure support team follows up with Darla on whether bulk-unenrolled completion certificates can be restored
- Send Darla the bulk unenrollment help guide

Customer:
- Wait for follow-up from Kevin/support team regarding certificate restoration
- Once restoration confirmed, bulk unenroll students from old/unpublished courses to get under the 5,000 active user limit

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD (Kevin to follow up ASAP by email; Darla offered to hop on another call)
- Materials to send: Bulk unenrollment help guide

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Darla came across as panicked and apologetic after the bulk unenrollment incident — she acted quickly without fully understanding the consequences. She is a conscientious, non-technical admin trying to do the right thing for her agency. This is a highly unusual government compliance use case: 18,500 "students" who are really licensees taking a single mandatory quiz once every two years. The platform functions essentially as a compliance-tracking tool. The certificate data loss is a genuine legal risk. High churn risk if certificates cannot be restored. Kevin appeared caught off-guard and had to escalate to support mid-call.

---

- Certificate Automation (~10:35) - "Now I lost all of their certificates of completion, which is what we need this for. I need to prove that they comply wit"
- Completion Tracking (~13:47) - "We audit all these licensees and we when we do our audits they're randomly selected. So let's say we select 500 of our l"

- Data Backup / Restore (~11:38) - "Is there a way to undo what I just did? Do you keep backups? Because I think I need all of that back."

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-17
ATTENDEES: Alejandro Esponda, Manuel Orvañanos, Marcelle Pipolo (Teachable SDR)
COMPANY: Alejandro Esponda / Manuel Orvañanos (company name not disclosed)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Alejandro Esponda and Manuel Orvañanos are building an online course platform to help students prepare for careers as professional athletes, likely based in Latin America (Spanish-speaking; LATAM payment methods discussed). They came prepared with a structured script of requirements and are actively evaluating Teachable. They are early stage — producing video content with a target launch in September/October 2026.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Create and sell self-paced online courses to train aspiring professional athletes.
Audience: Direct-to-consumer — aspiring professional athletes.
Business model: One-time course purchase.
Content types: Video courses; interest in quizzes, open-ended questions, and file upload for assignments.
Scale expectations: Not discussed — new to market.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Evaluating Growth plan (~$1,700/yr) vs. Premium plan ($6,500/yr with onboarding). Open to a White Glove Onboarding add-on (~$2,000–$2,500) if it can be attached to the lower plan — pending Zach approval.
Authority: Both attendees appear to be co-decision-makers; Marcelle Pipolo (Teachable) was the referring contact.
Need: Strong — actively producing video content with a firm launch timeline.
Timeline: September–October 2026 launch target.

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Affiliate/referral system (called out as a key requirement from their pre-call script).
Reporting needs: Not discussed.
Payments / checkout: One-time purchase model; LATAM local payment methods are relevant (Teachable mentioned upcoming LatAm payment support).
Admin or seat management: Not discussed.
Special workflows or constraints: Spanish-language landing page required.

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Came to the call with a prepared script of questions, indicating serious evaluation intent.
- Requested and enthusiastically accepted trial account offer.
- Expressed satisfaction throughout the demo ("That's perfect," "Sounds great," "No, we're very happy with that service actually.").
- Proactively asked about White Glove Onboarding pricing to accelerate course setup.
- Asked detailed questions about both pricing plans and whether add-ons were possible.
- Stated a concrete launch timeline (September/October 2026).

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Price sticker shock: Alejandro reacted to $6,500 ("600. $600?") — may be accustomed to a lower budget.
- Inquired whether the onboarding consultant could be added to the cheaper Growth plan instead, suggesting they want the service but not the full Premium price.
- Company name not disclosed — limited firmographic data available for follow-up research.

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth (~$1,700/yr self-serve) and Premium ($6,500/yr with onboarding specialist included up to 6 weeks).
Discounts offered: None discussed.
Contract length discussed: Annual pricing for both plans mentioned.
Constraints or approvals needed: Zach to check if onboarding add-on ($2,000–$2,500) can be approved for Growth plan customers.

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Send recap email with plan options, pricing breakdown, and trial account link.
- Check internally if White Glove Onboarding add-on ($2,000–$2,500) can be offered on Growth plan.
- Follow up in ~2 weeks to check progress.

Customer:
- Explore trial account.
- Continue producing video content for September/October launch.

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Informally ~2 weeks out (not formally booked).
- Materials to send: Recap email, plan comparison, trial account link.

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Both prospects appeared to be Spanish-speaking (they prepared a script possibly to overcome language/communication barriers). Marcelle Pipolo (Teachable) was the SDR who referred them and had given them a preview of pricing options. Prospects were polite, enthusiastic, and engaged throughout. The $6,500 sticker reaction suggests their target price point may be closer to the Growth plan. A Growth + add-on scenario (~$3,700–$4,200 total) could be the sweet spot to close this deal.

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Online Course Delivery (~5:15) - "No, we're very happy with that service actually."
- Affiliate / Referral Program (~1:45) - "Okay. Sounds great."
- One-time Payment Option (~2:45) - "Single purchase."
- File Upload & Grading (~4:30) - "That's perfect."
- White Glove Onboarding (~5:00) - "Marcel had previously mentioned about some kind of consulting onboarding service to help us to structure and set up all "
- Multi-language Support (~9:00) - "Would it be possible to have our landing page probably in Spanish? Is that something teachable?"

CALL DATE: 2026-06-17
ATTENDEES: Steven D'Agustino (Fordham University), Graham Johnson (Fordham University)
COMPANY: Fordham University
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Fordham University's Senior Director for Online Programs (Steven D'Agustino) and Instructional Designer (Graham Johnson) are exploring Teachable as an external platform to launch new micro-credentialing and continuing professional education (CPE) programs for external learners — a new initiative entirely outside Fordham's existing IT infrastructure. The graduate schools of law, social work, education, and business are interested in CPE programs tied to professional licensure (CLE, CFE, CTEs, etc.). They are early in evaluation with a target launch of end of August / September.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Build an external micro-credentialing and CPE platform for professional learners, separate from Fordham's internal MFA-gated LMS
Audience: External professionals needing CE credits for licensure (law, social work, education, business) and general learners seeking stackable non-credit credentials
Business model: Course sales with payment at checkout; memberships/subscriptions possible for some content types
Content types: Videos, PDFs, quizzes; live sessions potentially
Scale expectations: Starting from zero — no existing offerings in this space

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed
Authority: Steven reports to a Vice Provost; decision involves a broader group including the Vice Provost
Need: Strong — Fordham's existing LMS requires 24+ hours of MFA setup, discouraging external learners from enrolling; that friction is the primary driver for seeking an external platform
Timeline: End of August / September launch target

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Credly (asked about badge/certificate integration), WordPress (existing site)
Reporting needs: Course-level learner analytics (enrollments, completion rates), organization-level reporting for school administrators
Payments / checkout: Stripe, PayPal, Buy Now Pay Later (Afterpay, Klarna) discussed; Graham asked about payment systems
Admin or seat management: Organizations feature noted — school-level admins wanting their own portal and reporting
Special workflows or constraints: WCAG accessibility compliance required (captioning, screen reader); video scrub prevention needed for CE/CLE compliance; certificate/badge issuance on completion; must run entirely outside Fordham IT/SSO infrastructure; PDF accessibility validation is a gap

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Steven confirmed "Exactly, that's exactly what we're looking for" when Zach described professional credentialing as Teachable's sweet spot
- Concrete launch timeline of end of August / September
- Graham asked detailed technical questions (PDF accessibility checker, payment systems) indicating serious hands-on evaluation
- Law school is already asking internal questions about video scrub prevention — signals internal stakeholder engagement
- Steven asked about Teachable's longevity ("How long has Teachable been around?") — trust/stability vetting

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Vice Provost (key decision-maker) just went on vacation for 2 weeks; Steven also leaving next week — ~3-week decision pause
- Certificate system is proprietary to Teachable and not integrated with Credly/Open Badge standard — may not meet Fordham's digital badge requirements
- No built-in PDF accessibility checker — flagged as a gap by instructional designer Graham Johnson
- University procurement process adds institutional complexity beyond a standard SMB deal
- Steven noted they are evaluating "many ways into this market" — not exclusively focused on Teachable

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Video scrub prevention: Steven flagged an active internal question from the law school — strong signal for CLE compliance use case
- Certificate template gallery reacted to positively by Steven
- AI quiz generation: Steven engaged when Zach demonstrated it; asked clarifying questions about whether it is Teachable's own system

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth ($1,700/yr, 50 courses, self-serve) and Premium ($6,500/yr, 200 courses, white glove onboarding + account manager)
Discounts offered: None
Contract length discussed: Not discussed
Constraints or approvals needed: Vice Provost approval implied

- Follow up week of July 6th when Steven returns from vacation
