CALL DATE: 2026-06-17
ATTENDEES: Steven D'Agustino (Fordham University), Graham Johnson (Fordham University)
COMPANY: Fordham University
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Fordham University is exploring an external CE platform for non-credit professional programs (CLE, CFE, and related licensure credits) across their law, social work, business, and education graduate schools. They need a solution entirely separate from Fordham's existing IT infrastructure — their current LMS provisioning takes 24+ hours and is actively losing prospective learners who give up before getting access. They are at early discovery, evaluating multiple platforms, and targeting an end-of-August / September launch.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Build an end-to-end CE platform — course catalog/landing page, payment collection, immediate learner access, and badge/certificate issuance — for professionals who need to maintain licensure
Audience: Practicing professionals (lawyers, social workers, educators, business professionals) who need CE credits to maintain licenses
Business model: Revenue-generating; external professionals pay per course or program
Content types: Video-based courses, PDFs, potentially live sessions; CE programs with completion verification and compliance controls
Scale expectations: Multiple graduate schools (law, social work, business, education); starting with pilot programs; interested in stackable micro-credentials that can feed into degree pathways

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed explicitly; Zach mentioned Growth (~$1,700/yr) and Premium (~$6,500/yr) plans
Authority: Steven reports to a vice provost; decision will involve internal group buy-in; vice provost currently on vacation for ~2 weeks
Need: High — current LMS friction is actively deterring prospective learners from enrolling
Timeline: End of August / September target launch; Steven returns from vacation July 6th

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Custom domain / full white-label branding; potential embedding into existing Fordham/WordPress web presence; API for CRM/data export
Reporting needs: Per-course analytics (enrollments, completion rates); per-student tracking; school-level admin portal for principals/deans
Payments / checkout: Stripe, PayPal, Google Pay, Afterpay/Klarna; need immediate access upon payment without complex provisioning
Admin or seat management: Organization-level portal for school admins (principals/deans) to view group progress and enrollments
Special workflows or constraints: Must operate outside Fordham IT/SSO infrastructure; WCAG accessibility compliance required; video scrub prevention required for law school CE compliance; built-in PDF accessibility checker requested (currently unavailable in Teachable)

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- "That's exactly, that's exactly what we're looking for." — enthusiastic alignment when Zach described professional credentialing as Teachable's sweet spot
- End-of-August/September launch timeline stated explicitly — real urgency despite summer schedule delays
- Positive brand impression: "I think Teachable is a great name. We've met with a few and they have very weird names."
- Law school stakeholder already asking about video scrub prevention — multiple internal stakeholders engaged beyond just the champion
- Steven will report back to internal group, confirming active evaluation and champion role

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Evaluating multiple platforms ("we've met with a few") — competitive evaluation in progress
- Decision requires vice provost approval and internal group buy-in — timeline delayed by summer vacations
- University governance adds process complexity ("this is a university, so we have to be aware of other levels of complexity")
- Teachable doesn't offer market analytics or course idea generation — Steven asked, accepted the limitation, but noted as a gap
- PDF accessibility checker not built into Teachable — potential compliance concern for a university deploying to diverse learners

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Built-in PDF accessibility checker requested — not currently available; Zach confirmed PDFs are served as-uploaded with no in-platform accessibility checking
- Interest in Credly integration for digital badges — Teachable native certificates appear to suffice, but worth confirming if their credentialing workflows require Credly's Open Badge standard

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth (~$1,700/yr, 50 courses, self-serve) vs. Premium (~$6,500/yr, 200 courses, white glove onboarding + account manager)
Discounts offered: None mentioned
Contract length discussed: Not discussed
Constraints or approvals needed: Vice provost likely needs to sign off on vendor decision

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:

- Follow up week of July 6th when Steven returns from vacation

Customer:

- Reconnect week of July 6th with a sense of direction

CALL DATE: 2026-06-16
ATTENDEES: Dani Fairhurst, Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Dani Fairhurst
STAGE: Followup

---
SUMMARY
Dani Fairhurst is an existing Teachable customer on the Advanced Plan with significant overages — 21,000+ active students and 11,000+ imports vs. plan limits of 10,000 and 2,000 respectively. Kevin reached out to present two solutions — a custom unlimited-student plan at ~$650/mo or a switch to Teachable Pay — ahead of the June 25th renewal, when overage fees of ~$5,400/mo would otherwise kick in.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Continue hosting and selling online courses (evergreen + live launches)
Audience: Paying students (21,000+ active)
Business model: Course sales via live launches and evergreen funnels with paid ad traffic
Content types: Video courses, PDFs/digital downloads
Scale expectations: High — email list grew 30,000 in 9 months; expecting continued student volume increases

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Finance team controls; custom plan ~$650/mo or waived monthly fee with Teachable Pay discussed; current overage exposure ~$5,400/mo
Authority: Dani is evaluating but finance team makes the final decision
Need: High — currently over plan limits with costly overages looming
Timeline: Must decide before June 25, 2026 (renewal date)

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: ThriveCart (current checkout via API), Squarespace (website), ActiveCampaign (email); considering switch to Teachable Pay
Reporting needs: Google ad tracking on checkout and sales pages; A/B testing checkout vs. sales page conversion
Payments / checkout: Must support order bumps, upsells, and downsells
Admin or seat management: N/A
Special workflows or constraints: Finance team approval required for any pricing change

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Responded "Amazing" to unlimited student enrollment and waived monthly fee proposal
- Committed to testing Teachable checkout functionality herself before the decision
- Asked for everything in writing to pass to finance — actively moving process forward

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Finance team is the decision-maker; Dani cannot approve spend unilaterally
- Needs to verify Teachable checkout has feature parity with ThriveCart (order bumps, upsells, downsells, conversion tracking)
- Could stay on current plan with overages if checkout functionality doesn't meet requirements

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Custom plan at ~$650/mo (unlimited students) OR Teachable Pay with waived monthly subscription fee
Discounts offered: Overage fees waived if deal closes before June 25; cash back up to $6,500 if revenue exceeds $100K in first 6 months on Teachable Pay
Contract length discussed: Annual
Constraints or approvals needed: Finance team approval required

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send written summary: custom plan options, Teachable Pay pricing, overage fee breakdown (~$5,400/mo), cash back incentive details
- Include link to Teachable checkout demo/documentation

Customer:
- Dani to review and test Teachable checkout functionality
- Dani to forward proposal to finance team for approval

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD (likely email follow-up first)
- Materials to send: Full written proposal with all pricing options

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Dani is tech-savvy and manages their full stack (Squarespace, ThriveCart, Teachable, ActiveCampaign). Company is US-based (NY + CA) but Dani is UK-based. The overage fees create natural urgency — framing this as cost savings vs. $5,400/mo penalty is the right angle for the finance team pitch.

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- Multi-format Content Upload (~4:00) - "Are there any limits on like uploading of things? Uploading videos and PDFs and stuff like that?"
- Checkout / Sales Page UX (~5:30) - "do you have like order bumps and upsells and downsells and all that kind of like functionality in there?"
- Sales Funnel Analytics (~6:30) - "we run different ad campaigns. Sometimes we drive people straight to checkout, sometimes we drive them to a sales page. "
- Unlimited Student Enrollment (~4:30) - "Amazing."

CALL DATE: 2026-06-16
ATTENDEES: Jenny (email unknown), Amanda Smith (email unknown), Christy (email unknown)
COMPANY: Marcelle (company name inferred from call title; not confirmed in transcript)
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Jenny and Amanda represent a training organization currently on Docebo, seeking a simpler platform to replace it. They previously used Teachable before migrating to Docebo and are evaluating a return. They have four courses mixing free and paid content, instructor-led sessions organized by location-based quarterly cohorts, and a September 2026 launch deadline driving real urgency.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Replace Docebo with a simpler platform that still covers certification tracking, SCORM content import, and location-based student grouping
Audience: External learners and organizations (B2B group purchases + individual enrollment); locations include Lansing and Grand Rapids
Business model: Mix of free and paid courses at different price points; group and individual enrollment; resell content
Content types: Pre-built SCORM files, instructor-led sessions (Zoom and in-person), 12-week quarter-based cohorts
Scale expectations: ~100 students per quarter; 4 current courses; September 2026 new cohort launch

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Discussed $7,500/year (Premium plan); no price objection raised; multi-year discount of $500/year mentioned
Authority: Jenny is the primary contact and lead; Amanda Smith and Christy also involved in evaluation
Need: Strong — SCORM content already built, certifications required with unique IDs, September deadline creates urgency
Timeline: New courses start September 2026; targeting live by early August 2026

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: SCORM import (critical, noted as Q3 roadmap item); Constant Contact email integration; MailChimp mentioned as alternative
Reporting needs: Robust student completion tracking; certificate export with unique IDs; per-student and per-course reporting
Payments / checkout: Mix of free and paid courses; discount codes; member-only pricing tiers; group/bulk purchasing by organizations (invoice billing noted as coming soon)
Admin or seat management: Multiple admin levels (teacher/instructor, supervisor); location-based student grouping (Lansing group, Grand Rapids group as separate org units)
Special workflows or constraints: Automated email triggers at specific course progress milestones (not just pre-built triggers); student migration from Docebo at launch

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Prospect has a defined requirements checklist and offered to share it with Zach for a structured evaluation
- September 2026 course launch creates a hard deadline, driving timely decision
- Previously used Teachable — familiarity reduces onboarding friction
- No sticker shock on $7,500/year pricing; asked follow-up questions rather than pushing back
- Scheduled follow-up for June 24 at 4:00 PM Eastern before call ended

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- SCORM import not yet live (Q3 target); explicit concern raised by Jenny about inability to import existing course files — hard blocker if timeline slips past August
- Custom email triggers at arbitrary course progress points require third-party tool (MailChimp/Constant Contact); may be seen as a gap vs. Docebo
- Prospect previously left Teachable for Docebo — reason for original departure unknown; Amanda's SCORM question implies it was a capability gap

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Jenny explicitly flagged SCORM import as the top concern: "I'm concerned about not being able to input our scorm files for our courses that we have built out."
- Custom email notification triggers (beyond pre-built) viewed as a gap — prospect wants in-platform control without relying on MailChimp integration

---

Plan discussed: Premium plan at $7,500/year (up to 50,000 students, 2TB storage, 200 products)

- Research Constant Contact integration compatibility
- Send call recording and written recap
- Complete prospect's requirements checklist

Customer:

- Materials to send: Requirements checklist (from prospect), call recording, SCORM timeline update

---
SUMMARY
Jenny and her team are actively switching from Docebo to a simpler LMS that still covers their core requirements: SCORM import, certifications with unique IDs, quizzes, student file uploads, and multi-location cohort management. They sell training content externally to organizations (bulk/group purchase) and individuals across free and paid tiers. Their September new-cohort launch creates a hard deadline with real urgency.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Replace Docebo with a less complex platform supporting concurrent instructor-led cohorts at multiple Michigan locations (Lansing, Grand Rapids)
Audience: Employees of corporate clients (group/org purchase) and individual learners
Business model: Mixed — free courses plus paid courses at multiple price points; member-only pricing tier desired; content is sold externally
Content types: Existing SCORM files (must-have), in-person and Zoom instructor-led sessions, quizzes, student file-upload assignments
Scale expectations: 4 courses currently, 2–4 concurrent cohorts per course, quarter-based scheduling cycle

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Not discussed
Authority: Jenny is leading evaluation; Amanda Smith and Christy are team stakeholders
Need: High — actively migrating from Docebo, need new system live before September
Timeline: September 2026 new course start; Zach targeted early August for go-live

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Stripe (confirmed); mobile app (iOS/Android confirmed); SCORM import (critical blocker — Teachable Q3 roadmap)
Reporting needs: Robust student completion tracking; certification data export; org-level reporting per location cohort
Payments / checkout: Free and paid courses, discount codes, member-only pricing, group/bulk org purchase; invoice billing needed for B2B (not yet live in Teachable)
Admin or seat management: Multi-level admin (teacher/supervisor/org admin); separate reporting per location-based cohort group
Special workflows or constraints: SCORM import (in development, Q3); location-based cohort grouping (Lansing, Grand Rapids concurrent sessions); certifications with unique identifier codes; mixed enrollment (individual and group)

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Asked detailed questions about registration flow, payment processors, and mobile — indicates active, informed evaluation
- Confirmed hard September launch deadline and sought feasibility confirmation on timeline
- Raised SCORM concern directly and twice — sign of serious technical vetting, not casual exploration

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- SCORM import not yet available (Q3 Teachable roadmap) — Jenny flagged this explicitly as a concern; it is a must-have
- Invoice billing not yet live — needed for corporate group purchasing (Teachable noted it's coming EOY)
- Cohort/location grouping within Organizations feature was not immediately intuitive — Jenny expressed confusion during demo

- "Instructor per session" terminology doesn't map cleanly to Teachable's org admin role model; team uses session-based language throughout

---

Sebastian Estala is the co-founder of Film Dispatch, a San Diego-based film and content creation education brand transitioning from in-person events and workshops to digital courses. Primary goal: Host and sell self-paced filmmaking and content creation courses to a global audience, bridging their in-person event community to digital.

Business model: Course sales (one-time, potentially subscription/membership), in-person event/digital course flywheel, partnerships with cinematographers and influencers for co-created courses.

SUMMARY
Sebastian Estala is the founder of Film Dispatch, a filmmaking and content creation education company transitioning from in-person workshops (San Diego, LA, Tijuana, Mexico City) to a digital course platform. calls.title: Jeremy Shepherd and Kevin Codde
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-16
ATTENDEES: Jeremy Shepherd (Pearl Association of America), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Pearl Association of America
STAGE: Followup

---
SUMMARY
Jeremy Shepherd is the key decision-maker at Pearl Association of America, a nonprofit that has maintained 10 separate Teachable accounts across different languages (Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, French, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, German) to serve a global audience. He is actively relaunching their pearl education courses and evaluating whether to consolidate on Teachable or switch to LearnWorlds, Thinkific, or LearnDash, with the annual renewal decision due this month. The call ended with a plan to test Google Cloud Translation via Zapier as a workaround for multi-language support in a single account.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Consolidate 10 language-specific Teachable accounts into a single account using a multi-language translation integration, while relaunching updated pearl education courses
Audience: External learners interested in pearl/gemstone education; previously served 90,000 free signups via French Polynesia government sponsorship
Business model: Nonprofit; historically funded by the French Polynesia government (now lapsed); restarting active course promotion
Content types: Video-based pearl education courses manually translated across 10 languages
Scale expectations: Only a few hundred active students currently; Growth plan (5,000 active student limit) is sufficient for their needs

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Annual operating budget ~$32,000; current single-account Teachable spend ~$1,100/year but running 10 accounts has been proportionally expensive
Authority: Jeremy is the decision-maker
Need: High — multi-language consolidation is the critical requirement; renewal decision point is now
Timeline: Decision required this month (literal annual renewal)

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Google Cloud Translation via Zapier (or Weglot) for multi-language support in a single account
Reporting needs: Not discussed
Payments / checkout: Not discussed beyond plan pricing
Admin or seat management: Needs to mass-unenroll ~87,000 inactive students and consolidate student databases from 10 accounts into one via CSV export/import
Special workflows or constraints: Wants a re-engagement email campaign for relaunched courses; concerned about losing historical student comment/conversation data if migrating to another platform

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Committed to testing Google Cloud Translation + Zapier integration before the renewal deadline
- Explicitly aligned with Kevin on next steps at close of call
- Main retention reason explicitly stated: existing student history and data already in Teachable
- Decision is due literally this month and course relaunch is already underway

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- LearnWorlds natively solves multi-language in a single account; Thinkific also covers all but Vietnamese
- Jeremy was annoyed by an unexpected overage email that nearly pushed him to switch before this call
- Teachable's native student-facing language dropdown may not be fully live, causing confusion with a marketing email Jeremy received
- Google Cloud Translation via Zapier may not handle the logged-in course experience cleanly; Jeremy explicitly flagged this risk
- Additional cost of translation workaround (~$200/year) adds friction vs. competitors' native solution

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK

calls.title: Meeting with Teachable
calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-16
ATTENDEES: Thaksapohn Peerapatpokin, Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Thaksapohn Peerapatpokin
STAGE: Followup

---
SUMMARY
Existing Teachable customer based in Thailand with ~1,000 students running a personal online teaching school. Called to resolve import limit overages on Growth plan; agreed to upgrade to Advanced plan (4,000 imports) with overage fees waived and future payment deferred to April renewal.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Archive live Facebook teaching sessions on Teachable so students can watch recordings after Facebook deletes them at one month
Audience: ~1,000 Thai students; 500-600 enrolled per new course launch
Business model: Paid online courses collected via bank transfer (Stripe not suitable for Thai market)
Content types: Video recordings (originally livestreamed on Facebook)
Scale expectations: Opens new courses periodically; expects ~500-600 import events per new course

---
QUALIFICATION
Need: Higher import capacity without full plan upgrade; local payment method support for Thailand
Timeline: Plan renews April 29th

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Payments / checkout: Uses bank transfer; open to exploring Teachable Pay but uncertain if Stripe is suitable for Thai students
Special workflows or constraints: Re-enrolls existing students into new courses via bulk import; each per-course enrollment counted as a new import event

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Agreed immediately to upgrade to Advanced plan
- Expressed strong positive sentiment: "Teachable is a great platform so far. I love using it."

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Stripe/Teachable Pay may not be suitable for Thai students; bank transfer is strongly preferred
- If import volumes exceed 4,000 on Advanced plan, will need a further custom arrangement

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Videos freeze after 30-40 minutes of playback in browser; students must refresh to continue — directed to support@teachable.com

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Advanced plan at $309/month (annual billing)
Discounts offered: Overage fees waived; import limit extended from standard 2,000 to 4,000
Contract length discussed: Annual
Constraints or approvals needed: None — customer agreed on the call

---
NEXT STEPS
Customer:
- Review Teachable Pay documentation sent by Kevin
- Sign DocuSign contract for Advanced plan upgrade

Scheduled:
- Kevin to send DocuSign contract with overage fee waiver and 4,000 import limit
- Next payment: April 29th

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Highly satisfied existing customer; quick, frictionless upgrade. Primary expansion risk is Stripe/Teachable Pay adoption in Thai market. Video streaming bug (freezing at 30-40 min mark) flagged — support follow-up needed. No company name stated; appears to be a personal-brand online school.

---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- International Payment Processing (~2:30) - "So I am in Thailand and actually it is not quite comfortable for my students to pay via like you have stripe, right? And"
- SMB / Flexible Pricing Tiers (~3:30) - "Are there any customized plan for something like stick with the growth but add more important users in this plan?"
---
FEATURE REQUESTS
- International Payment Processing (~2:30) - "So I am in Thailand and actually it is not quite comfortable for my students to pay via like you have stripe, right? And"
- SMB / Flexible Pricing Tiers (~3:30) - "Are there any customized plan for something like stick with the growth but add more important users in this plan?"

---
SUMMARY
Ela Thier (IFS) is an existing Teachable Growth plan customer who exceeded active student limits (10,000+ vs. 5,000 allowed) and annual import limits, triggering overage charges. Kevin Codde reached out to discuss upgrade options: either the Advanced plan ($309/month, 13,000 students) or migration to Teachable Pay (unlimited students, competitive transaction fees). Ela is interested but mid-launch and will revisit in ~2 weeks.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Run a bundled all-access membership course business at $97/month
Audience: Consumers purchasing online courses via a recurring membership
Business model: Recurring membership payments through ThriveCart; course content hosted on Teachable
Content types: Dozens of self-paced courses including orientation gating + full course library unlock
Scale expectations: 10,000+ active students; continuing to grow

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Currently paying $189/month; aware of $309/month Advanced option; Teachable Pay would keep current plan cost
Authority: Ela is the decision-maker; automation specialist not on call must review migration
Need: Over student limit causing overage fees; membership pause/cancel UX is broken across ThriveCart+Teachable split
Timeline: Mid-launch now; reviewing options in ~2 weeks

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: ThriveCart for payments alongside Teachable for content; potential migration to Teachable Pay
Reporting needs: Transaction search and export is clunky — hard to filter students by payment status (defaulted vs. paid)
Payments / checkout: Open to Teachable Pay if fee comparison is favorable; needs concrete fee numbers first
Admin or seat management: 10,000+ active students vs. 5,000 limit; 2,000 imports vs. 1,000 annual limit
Special workflows or constraints: Orientation gating + bulk course unlock not supported by current Learning Paths feature (sequential-only). Mobile app forces completion-order display — students are being redirected to browser instead.

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Open to migrating to Teachable Pay if fees are competitive
- Interested in Advanced plan if overage fees are waived as part of the deal
- Lauren stated they are "good to move forward once we get the email"
- Ela agreed to share ThriveCart transaction fees for comparison

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Mid-launch: no bandwidth to evaluate for ~2 weeks
- Automation specialist (not on call) must approve any migration from ThriveCart
- Membership pause/cancel UX is a hard requirement — if Teachable Pay doesn’t solve it, deal may stall
- No intermediate pricing tier between 5,000 and 10,000 students was a friction point
- Mobile app course ordering bug was previously a near-churn event

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Teachable mobile app overrides creator-curated course order, showing completion order instead — actively harmful; Ela is redirecting all mobile users to browser
- Transaction record search and export in Teachable is clunky; can’t easily filter by payment status (defaulted vs. paid); required manual workarounds
- Membership cancellation and pause flow is broken when content is on Teachable and payments are on ThriveCart
- Original reason for moving to ThriveCart was checkout page flexibility (Ela noted details are fuzzy)

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Advanced Plan ($309/mo, 13,000 students) and Teachable Pay (unlimited students, current plan price)
Discounts offered: Overage fees waived under either option
Contract length discussed: Currently monthly; can remain monthly
Constraints or approvals needed: Need ThriveCart fee comparison before Teachable Pay offer can be finalized; automation specialist review required for migration

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- Send written comparison of both options (Advanced at $309/mo with 13k students vs. Teachable Pay with unlimited)
- Include current overage charge amount in email
- Confirm membership pause/cancel capability on Teachable Pay
- Return with Teachable Pay transaction rate once Ela shares ThriveCart fees

Customer:
- Share ThriveCart transaction fee rates
- Review options with automation specialist post-launch
- Circle back in ~2 weeks to decide

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD (~2 weeks after launch)
- Materials to send: Written options comparison + overage charge breakdown

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Ela is an experienced creator with a well-established membership business (10k+ students, $97/month). She is data-driven and wants concrete numbers before any decision. The mobile app ordering bug was a near-churn event — she mentioned internal discussions about leaving Teachable because of it. Tone was collaborative and constructive. Lauren handles operational details and seems ready to move forward once the email lands.

---

- Membership / Subscription Pricing (~13:00) - "would students have an easy cancel and pause option?"
- Checkout / Sales Page UX (~6:00) - "I think there was just a lot more flexibility in terms of what we could do in checkout pages."
- Reporting Data Export (CSV) (~5:00) - "it's hard to find, you know, students who've defaulted versus students who've paid exporting. Exporting records becomes "
- Course Sequencing / Completion Gating (~15:00) - "we do want them to finish the orientation modules before they unlock all the courses, but once they finish that, we want"
- Mobile App Course Delivery (~13:30) - "The Teachable app is not usable because we can't default to the course creators...the Teachable app forces your order in"
- SMB / Flexible Pricing Tiers (~9:00) - "is it just 5,000, 10,000 or there's no like in between monthly plan for that... there's not like an 8,000 like Happy Med"

CALL DATE: 2026-06-15
ATTENDEES: Bekhruz Khazratov (help@featuresolicitor.co.uk), Kevin Codde
COMPANY: Feature Solicitor
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
Feature Solicitor is a small UK-based exam prep company that uses Teachable as an API-driven headless backend to deliver recorded videos and study materials to external subscribers; their subscription billing and mock exams live on a WordPress front-end. The call was initiated to resolve account overages (exceeded Growth plan import and active-student limits) and negotiate an upgrade to a custom Advanced plan.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: API-driven delivery of video courses and exam prep content to paying subscribers
Audience: External learners (consumers) preparing for professional exams
Business model: Monthly subscription and 7-day free trial; Teachable serves strictly as the course delivery backend, not a storefront
Content types: Recorded videos, PM slides; mock exams (thousands of multiple-choice questions) hosted on WordPress via GitHub Actions
Scale expectations: ~2,300 API imports per year; at most ~100 actively enrolled students at any point; 9,000+ total user records accumulated

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Currently on Growth plan; evaluating Advanced (custom) at $309/mo (annual) or $399/mo (monthly) for 3,000 imports and 12,000 active students; $500/mo discussed for 5,000 imports and 20,000 students if they grow faster
Authority: Bekhruz is co-founder but must consult business partner Tom before committing
Need: Overage resolution (exceeded 1,000 import and 5,000 active-student limits on Growth); needs clarity on active-student definition and higher custom limits
Timeline: Waiting for Kevin's written proposal; Tom to review before deciding — likely within days

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: Heavy API usage — account creation, enrollment, and unenrollment all driven via Teachable API; GitHub Actions for WordPress content pipeline
Reporting needs: Not discussed
Payments / checkout: Handled externally on WordPress; not Teachable
Admin or seat management: Needs a clear definition of "active student" (enrolled vs. unenrolled); wants 3,000 imports and 12,000 active students on custom Advanced plan
Special workflows or constraints: 7-day free trial cycle — students enrolled via API then unenrolled; ensures very few truly active enrollments at any moment despite large total user count

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Beck acknowledged it would be "very expensive" to switch platforms at this stage — deeply locked in via API
- Leaning toward accepting the 12,000 student / 3,000 import custom offer; said it "sounds good"
- Actively doing math on whether current usage would fit within proposed limits, indicating real engagement with the offer

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Needs business partner Tom's sign-off before committing; Tom dropped off the call without participating
- Concerned about long-term import/student caps if growth accelerates; asked about a higher tier (20,000 students / 5,000 imports) proactively

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Custom Advanced plan (3,000 imports, 12,000 active students)
Discounts offered: Overage waiver + refund if upgrade signed; custom limits above published Advanced plan
Contract length discussed: Annual ($309/mo) vs. monthly ($399/mo); $500/mo for even higher limits
Constraints or approvals needed: Tom (business partner) must approve before contract is signed

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- N/A (Kevin Codde's account)

Customer:
- Beck and Tom to review and respond to Kevin's written proposal

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: None set; async via email
- Materials to send: Kevin to send written contract detailing overage waiver and new custom plan limits

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Existing customer — retention / expansion call, not new prospect. Small UK company; very API-first and infrastructure-minded (treats Teachable as a backend, not a front-end product). Sticky because migration would be costly. Somewhat price-sensitive (two co-founders, small team). Beck was collegial, technically sharp, and reasonable; likely to close pending Tom's approval. Note: call duration logged as 0 min in Fireflies, but transcript is clearly ~12-15 min.

CALL DATE: 2026-06-12
ATTENDEES: Federico Piovesan, Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Federico Piovesan (company name not provided in call)
STAGE: Discovery

---
SUMMARY
Federico Piovesan is part of a small Italian enterprise that provides training services and software development to corporate and public administration clients. For the first time, a client has asked them to deliver fully online, asynchronous training. He evaluated Teachable independently, is satisfied with the UX, and joined this call to confirm GDPR compliance and explore enterprise features available on lower plans before committing.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Deliver fully online asynchronous training content to a client's employees
Audience: Corporate employees of one client (~40-50 students for initial project)
Business model: B2B training services provider; not selling courses directly to consumers
Content types: Pre-recorded content, presentations, and course materials
Scale expectations: 40-50 students for current project; potential growth if online training expands to more clients

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Starting with Starter plan; open to upgrading to Builder; stated $5,000/year for custom enterprise plan is "not unthinkable" if they push online training further
Authority: Federico appears to be the evaluator and decision-maker for the company
Need: First online training project; GDPR compliance required for future public administration clients
Timeline: Platform test live in early autumn; full student access by end of 2026

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: None mentioned
Reporting needs: Organization-level reporting (he confirmed this was a prior question)
Payments / checkout: Not applicable — not selling courses to individuals
Admin or seat management: Organization hierarchy and group management (enterprise feature, relevant for future use)
Special workflows or constraints: GDPR compliance documentation required; needs DPA and full sub-processor list; Course Sequencing / Completion Gating for structured asynchronous delivery

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Already tested the platform independently: "in terms of UX and functionalities, I'm pretty satisfied with it"
- Ready to proceed with Starter or Builder plan for initial project
- Confirmed $5,000/year for a custom plan "is not unthinkable" if online training grows
- Specifically requested sub-processor list and DPA via email — indicates active vendor evaluation for compliance due diligence

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- GDPR sub-processor documentation is a potential blocker, especially for future public administration clients; needs DPA and full vendor list
- Large pricing gap between Educator and Enterprise plans is a concern given the experimental nature of this initial project
- Deal depends on this first online training experiment succeeding — may not grow if the experiment doesn't lead to more client demand

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Teachable's usability praised strongly versus Moodle: "the usability is really, really limited, both from the teacher side and the student side" (referring to Moodle, which is common in Italy)

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Starter (initial); Builder (potential upgrade); Custom enterprise plan (~$5,000/year with dedicated CSM and onboarding)
Discounts offered: None mentioned
Contract length discussed: Not discussed
Constraints or approvals needed: GDPR compliance documentation must be reviewed before full commitment

---
NEXT STEPS
Kevin:
- Send sub-processor list and DPA documentation to Federico via email

Customer:
- Review sub-processor list and DPA
- Decide between Starter and Builder plan
- Begin producing training content for upload and test

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-11
ATTENDEES: Christine F (Mark Clayborne account admin), Mark Clayborne (absent — had webinar conflict)
COMPANY: Mark Clayborne
STAGE: Followup

---
SUMMARY
Christine F, who manages Mark Clayborne's Teachable account, joined in place of Mark to discuss an unexpected overage charge from hitting the imported student limit. The call resolved around the possibility of switching to Teachable Pay to eliminate import limits and receive a refund on the overage. Kevin Codde (Teachable CS) drove the conversation; this is an existing customer expansion/retention touchpoint, not a new sales call.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Offer free and paid online courses to software product members, trial users, and leads
Audience: External customers and trial users of their software product; inbound leads via MailerLite
Business model: Software company using courses as a customer conversion and onboarding tool; also sells paid Mastery class courses
Content types: Self-paced video courses (free and paid)
Scale expectations: ~1,000–1,500 imported students per year currently; wants to grow without per-import billing surprises

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: On existing plan; motivated to avoid overages and reduce cost
Authority: Christine is operational admin; Mark (account owner) and Rose (CEO, Mark's wife) handle billing decisions — neither was on this call
Need: Eliminate imported student billing limit; identify and delete inactive students; understand Teachable Pay mechanics
Timeline: Must decide before next billing cycle (end of month)

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: MailerLite + Zapier for lead enrollment; software API/Zapier for member enrollment
Reporting needs: Filterable list of which students counted as "imported" (charged); activity/login tracking to identify inactive users
Payments / checkout: Current processor unknown to Christine (needs to confirm with Mark — possibly PayPal or Stripe); evaluating switch to Teachable Pay
Admin or seat management: Wants bulk deletion capability for inactive students; some students have duplicate accounts
Special workflows or constraints: Free course access granted via Zapier enrollment or coupon codes; must confirm both workflows are compatible with Teachable Pay

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Christine confirmed they'd seriously consider switching to Teachable Pay to remove limits and recover the overage charge
- Expressed clear urgency — must decide before end-of-month billing
- Asked Kevin to send documentation and rate comparison for internal review with Mark and Rose
- Asked about minimum transaction threshold: indicates intent to commit if terms are clear

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Mark and Rose (CEO) were not on the call — billing decision requires their approval before anything can be signed
- Christine doesn't know current payment processor or rates — blocks the rate comparison Kevin needs to build a proposal
- Concern that deleting students might not reduce billed count if those users aren't in the "imported" bucket

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- No way to export or filter a list of which students were counted as "imported" (billed) — Christine asked for this twice; support team also couldn't help
- Using tags to manually track students across many courses is tedious and doesn't scale
- Student limit billing structure was confusing and unexpected — they didn't realize Zapier-enrolled students counted toward the cap

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Current plan with ~1,000 imported student cap; Teachable Pay unlocks unlimited
Discounts offered: Full overage refund contingent on switching all paid course payments to Teachable Pay
Contract length discussed: Ongoing agreement to use Teachable Pay for paid courses (not a fixed term)
Constraints or approvals needed: Mark and Rose must approve payment processor switch; must finalize before next billing date

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- (Not on this call — Kevin Codde handled)

Kevin:
- Send email with Teachable Pay overview, rate comparison vs. existing processor, and overage refund terms
- Follow up with support team on whether a list of imported/charged students can be pulled

Customer:
- Christine to ask Mark for current payment processor name and transaction rates
- Share Kevin's email with Mark and Rose for billing decision
- Reach back out if additional questions; set up follow-up call with Mark present if needed

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD (only if follow-up questions require Mark on the call)
- Materials to send: Teachable Pay overview + rate breakdown email from Kevin

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Three-person decision unit: Christine (operational), Mark (owner/course manager), Rose (CEO/billing). Christine is engaged and understands the issue but lacks signing authority. Medium-high urgency due to billing deadline. Kevin's offer of an overage refund is a strong lever if the proposal lands before end of month. Existing customer — retention and expansion opportunity.

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-11
ATTENDEES: Tracy Melancon (Louisiana Municipal Association), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Louisiana Municipal Association
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
Kevin called Tracy — LMA's long-tenured training administrator — about active student overage on their Growth plan. LMA is a nonprofit that provides free mandatory compliance training (cybersecurity and sexual harassment prevention) to employees of member municipalities across Louisiana. Certificates are required for legislature auditing. Tracy has been actively cleaning up stale users and is open to upgrading to the Advanced plan with a higher student limit.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Deliver free mandatory compliance training (cybersecurity, sexual harassment prevention) to employees of member cities, towns, and villages in Louisiana
Audience: Municipal employees whose employers are LMA member municipalities
Business model: Nonprofit; training is free to members; no revenue collected
Content types: Compliance courses with downloadable completion certificates; three trainings per year
Scale expectations: ~14,965 learners last year; hoping to maintain under 15,000 active students going forward

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Cost-sensitive nonprofit; per-seat LMS pricing is unaffordable; receptive to $3,200/yr on 2-year deal
Authority: Tracy must bring pricing options to LMA leadership before deciding — not the sole decision maker
Need: Immediate — account is in overage; renewal is September 2026
Timeline: September 2026 renewal; Tracy to present options to team after Kevin sends email

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: None mentioned
Reporting needs: Must track who completed training each year; certificates retained for 2 years for legislature auditing
Payments / checkout: Not applicable — all training is free
Admin or seat management: Needs higher student limit; open registration cannot be restricted; manual bulk cleanup is ongoing and burdensome
Special workflows or constraints: Learners use personal emails (Gmail, Yahoo), making membership verification and automated cleanup nearly impossible; cannot prevent non-members from registering

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Said "I believe so" when asked about signing a multi-year agreement
- 6-7 year tenure on the platform with no mention of evaluating alternatives
- Actively working to bring account into compliance — engaged and cooperative

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Requires leadership approval before committing to pricing; not a unilateral decision
- Frustrated that student limits were not clearly communicated at signup ("at the time it said unlimited")
- Nonprofit budget constraints; any price increase requires justification to leadership

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Open registration is a persistent pain point: cannot prevent non-members from joining despite front-page messaging
- Bulk user cleanup is burdensome and manual — users who joined with personal emails and churned from their municipalities are very hard to identify and remove

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Advanced plan with 30,000 active student limit
Discounts offered: $3,200/yr on 2-year agreement (vs. $3,708 standard/1-year)
Contract length discussed: 1-year at $3,708 vs. 2-year at $3,200
Constraints or approvals needed: Tracy must present both options to LMA leadership team

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- N/A (Kevin Codde's account)

Customer:
- Review pricing email from Kevin
- Present 1-year and 2-year options to LMA leadership
- Respond with decision before September 2026 renewal

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: Not set; follow-up via email
- Materials to send: Kevin to email both pricing options (1-year $3,708 / 2-year $3,200) and information on Access Duration auto-unenroll feature

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Long-tenured customer (6-7 years). Cooperative but clearly frustrated by the lack of transparency around student limits at original signup. Tracy is the platform admin but not the budget authority — needs to sell the upgrade internally. Open registration abuse and personal email usage are structural problems that make user management extremely difficult at scale. Auto-unenroll (Access Duration feature) could be a meaningful solution to surface during follow-up.

CALL DATE: 2026-06-10
ATTENDEES: Barbara Cox (National Ataxia Foundation), Amanda Araujo (Teachable), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: National Ataxia Foundation
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
The National Ataxia Foundation is a nonprofit supporting people with ataxia, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. Barbara Cox is evaluating Teachable to organize and deliver free educational content to thousands of members (patients and families), healthcare professionals (for CME), and internal staff. She experienced Teachable positively as a student and has existing brand affinity, but is actively comparing platforms and is very price-sensitive given the nonprofit's limited budget.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Deliver organized, self-paced courses and recorded webinars publicly to members and healthcare professionals (CME); secondarily onboard new employees and 65 support group leaders
Audience: External members (people with ataxia and families), healthcare professionals (neurologists, PTs, social workers, speech-language therapists, OTs), support group leaders, internal staff
Business model: Nonprofit — all content free to learners; no student-facing payments; CME delivery for healthcare professionals
Content types: Stored webinars (YouTube links), PDFs, short instructor videos; no live sessions planned on Teachable
Scale expectations: Starting under 25 courses; potential for 2,000+ active students if CME and professional programs launch

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: $5,400/yr with nonprofit discount (Core + 2,000 students); described as "a really big ask" for the nonprofit
Authority: Barbara is the evaluator/champion; unnamed female boss must approve; CME colleague manages that department separately
Need: Strong — need to organize scattered webinar library and build structured accessible course content
Timeline: Building free trial demo over next 2-3 days to show boss; no hard deadline but moving quickly

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: YouTube video linking for existing webinar content
Reporting needs: Basic student progress and completion tracking
Payments / checkout: No student-facing payments (all free); no payment processing required
Admin or seat management: Core + 2,000 active students at $5,400/yr; requested sample pricing for 5,000-student custom package
Special workflows or constraints: Requires fully open/public self-service enrollment — members must be able to register and access courses on their own at any time without manual assignment

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- All departments internally aligned ("they all said yeah, yeah, fine, we need it"); Barbara delegated to find the right platform
- Requested a live demo during the discovery call itself rather than scheduling a separate session
- Asked for a free trial sandbox to demo to boss alongside written recommendation
- Asked for custom pricing scenarios up to 5,000 students, indicating long-term planning
- Positive prior experience as a Teachable student (yoga course during COVID); strong brand affinity

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- Very price-sensitive nonprofit; $6,000/yr described as "a really big ask"; competitors offer unlimited courses and learner accounts at lower price
- Teachable's credit card requirement for free trial is a friction point; mentioned unprompted twice
- Actively comparing multiple platforms; competitor research ongoing
- CME requirements not explored in depth; separate CME colleague manages that program
- Boss approval required; timeline is uncertain

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Free trial friction: Credit card requirement is a competitive disadvantage vs. competitors that allow time-limited trials without CC
- Pricing/value: Teachable's price feels high relative to competitors offering unlimited students and courses
- Enrollment UX: Organization-based enrollment felt too manual for primary use case of open public member access

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Core package ($6,000/yr → $5,400/yr with nonprofit discount); 2,000 active students; Organizations feature included
Discounts offered: ~10% nonprofit discount ($6,000 → $5,400)
Contract length discussed: Annual; not specified further
Constraints or approvals needed: Boss approval required; Barbara building demo first

---

Kevin:
- Send follow-up email with: (1) Core + 2,000 students at $5,400/yr breakdown; (2) Sample custom package for 5,000 students

- Share Kevin's email with boss and present recommendation

- Next meeting date: Not scheduled; Barbara preferred email-only follow-up
- Materials to send: Kevin's pricing comparison email covering both packages

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-10
ATTENDEES: Barbara Cox (National Ataxia Foundation, email unknown), Amanda Araujo (Teachable), Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: National Ataxia Foundation
STAGE: Discovery / Demo

---
SUMMARY
Barbara Cox works at the National Ataxia Foundation — a national nonprofit supporting people with a rare neurodegenerative disease — and is evaluating Teachable to build a structured education hub for their members. The platform would host recorded webinars, condition-specific courses, and CME/CE training for healthcare professionals (neurologists, PTs, SLPs, OTs, social workers), all offered free of charge. She came in with specific questions about pricing, student limits, and free trial access after experiencing Teachable as a student through a yoga teacher during COVID.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Move their existing library of webinars and condition-specific educational content off an unstructured public website and into an organized, searchable course platform accessible to all members on demand
Audience: Members with ataxia and their families (primary); healthcare professionals for CME training (secondary); a small number of employees and 65 support group leaders
Business model: Non-revenue — all content is free to members; the foundation pays for the platform
Content types: Recorded webinars, YouTube video links, PDFs, short internal training videos (e.g., CEO welcome message)
Scale expectations: Starting with fewer than 25 courses; up to 2,000 members initially, potentially scaling to 5,000+ if healthcare professional CME is added

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Nonprofit budget — $6,000/year described as a "really big ask"; responded positively to nonprofit discount bringing to $5,400/year ($450/month); needs internal approval
Authority: Barbara is champion/evaluator but reports to a boss who has final say; CME department handled by a colleague
Need: Strong — clearly defined use case, existing content library ready, personally motivated
Timeline: Plans to build a demo course in the next few days to present to boss; no hard launch date; admin team currently busy with other projects

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Integrations: None mentioned; YouTube video links would be embedded
Reporting needs: Not discussed in depth

calls.hubspot_note:
CALL DATE: 2026-06-10
ATTENDEES: Andrea Wilson, Shayla Grady, Kevin Codde (Teachable)
COMPANY: Safe Sleep Education Nonprofit (company name not stated on call)
STAGE: Negotiation

---
SUMMARY
Existing customer retention call initiated by Teachable (Kevin Codde) to address a significant active student overage. The organization is a national nonprofit educating parents, caregivers, and health professionals about safe sleep for infants (SIDS prevention), offering free courses. They have 118,000 students in their account against a 5,000-student plan limit, and were not aware of the plan change from unlimited. The call centered on pricing options for renewal in July.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Free public health education on safe sleep for babies to prevent sleep-related deaths
Audience: Parents, caregivers, and health professionals across the country
Business model: Nonprofit; all courses are free
Content types: Educational courses (free, self-paced)
Scale expectations: ~32,000-33,000 new enrollments per year; 118,000 total students in system

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Major constraint — increase from ~$1,800/year to $6,600/year (or $5,000/year multi-year) is a significant jump for a nonprofit; requires internal approval
Authority: Andrea Wilson appears to be in leadership; referenced needing internal buy-in before committing
Need: Critical — their 33,000 annual enrollments are 6x their current plan limit; unlimited student access is core to their operations
Timeline: Plan renews July 2026

---
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Admin or seat management: Need to maintain access for 118,000+ students; deactivating accounts is not a viable workaround as students need ongoing access to completed training and downloadable certificates
Special workflows or constraints: Students must retain indefinite access to completed courses and certificates after finishing; this is a core promise to their learners

---
BUYING SIGNALS
- Actively engaged in renewal discussion; plan renews July 2026 — short window
- Asked specific questions about multi-year discount options
- Andrea engaged with the $5,000/year multi-year proposal rather than rejecting it outright

---
RISKS / OBJECTIONS
- 3-4x price increase is a potential dealbreaker for a budget-constrained nonprofit
- Customer feels misled: plan changed from unlimited to 5,000 students without their awareness ("we weren't aware that our plan went from unlimited down to 5,000")
- Requires internal approval before any commitment; may need to go to a board or leadership team
- If cost cannot be accommodated, they may seek a lower-cost or free alternative

---
PRODUCT FEEDBACK
- Deactivating students to manage overage is not viable — students need to access completed training and download certificates indefinitely
- The unlimited student promise was a key reason they chose Teachable; the plan change eroded trust

---
PRICING DISCUSSED
Plan discussed: Growth plan (currently at 5,000 student limit)
Discounts offered: Nonprofit discount — $550/mo (vs. $650/mo standard) for 150,000 student limit; $5,000/year with multi-year contract
Contract length discussed: Multi-year option proposed
Constraints or approvals needed: Internal approval required; budget decision pending

---
NEXT STEPS
Zach:
- (Kevin Codde is the rep on this call)
- Kevin to send written pricing proposal for Andrea to share internally
- Kevin to be main point of contact for follow-up questions

Customer:
- Andrea Wilson to discuss internally with team about cost increase and approval process

Scheduled:
- Next meeting date: TBD pending internal discussion
- Materials to send: Written pricing proposal from Kevin Codde

---
ADDITIONAL CONTEXT
Strong retention risk. The customer feels blindsided by a plan change that fundamentally altered their value proposition. They are a legitimate public-health nonprofit doing meaningful work. The gap between their actual usage (33K/year, 118K total) and their plan limit (5K) is extreme. Kevin handled it professionally and offered nonprofit pricing, but the 3-4x cost jump is significant. Gut feel: they will push back hard on price or seek alternatives if a workable nonprofit deal cannot be structured.

---

- Unlimited Student Enrollment (~1:15) - "We were under the impression we had unlimited when we signed up... we were relying on that kind of unlimited structure."
- Access Duration / Expiration (~2:45) - "If a student account is inactive, they're not going to be able to like, get back in there and re-access the training tha"
- Certification / Completion Certificates (~3:00) - "The perk thus far has been that, like, they can go back in, check back in on it, download their own certificate and ever"
- SMB / Flexible Pricing Tiers (~4:45) - "Obviously part of the reason we used your platform was the, the cost we were able to pay with the unlimited students."

---
SUMMARY
Shannon Rebelo runs an educationally focused nonprofit that delivers coaching programs and training content to external clients. She has been a Docebo customer for seven years and is actively switching away due to rising costs and platform bloat. She already has a Teachable free trial and has begun migrating content.

---
USE CASE
Primary goal: Replace Docebo with a simpler, more cost-effective LMS for delivering coaching programs and training content to external organizations.
Audience: External client organizations (B2B seat-licensed), individual coaching participants, masterclass attendees.
Business model: Licenses courses to organizations on a seat basis; runs live masterclasses; delivers storytelling/leadership coaching programs.
Content types: Online courses, coaching sessions (Zoom), live masterclasses, quizzes, certificates.
Scale expectations: Small-to-medium — up to 3 active client organizations at a time, sub-250 learner scale.

---
QUALIFICATION
Budget: Comparing Growth ($139/mo annual) vs Core (~$6,000/yr). The price gap is significant for a nonprofit.
Authority: Champion — needs to bring the decision back to her team. Not sole decision-maker.
Need: Strong — actively on Docebo, already migrating to Teachable free trial.
Timeline: Immediate — in active content migration.

---

Integrations: Zoom (for live masterclasses and coaching sessions).
Reporting needs: Student progress reports, quiz scores, org-level leaderboards; CSV export.
Payments / checkout: Not discussed.
Admin or seat management: Wants org-level admins who can self-manage their own group independently; wants to recycle org slots after 60-day access periods expire.
Special workflows or constraints: Wants to gate coaching sessions behind prior module completion; wants time-based drip for bi-weekly coaching cohorts (e.g., unlock next section 7 days after enrollment or after a scheduled session).

- Price gap between Growth ($139/mo) and Core (~$6,000/yr) may keep her on Growth, missing key enterprise features (Organizations, Learning Paths, SSO)
- Nonprofit budget likely constrained
- Team buy-in required before commitment; she is not the sole decision-maker

Discounts offered: None mentioned

Constraints or approvals needed: Team discussion required

Allen is a multi-location restaurant operator evaluating Teachable for employee training (cook training, host training). recap: This week's calls reveal a clear pattern: the continuing education / compliance training ICP is gaining traction across both internal strategy and external prospects. Dot Compliance (compliance training for commercial drivers) progressed from initial hands-on testing to detailed integration planning with all content uploaded. BADM (nonprofit) is ready to sign an Unlimited contract. Speravita (nonprofit pregnancy resource centers) brought Teachable's product team into a deep organizational scoping call with 115 centers and Q2 launch plans. The Singapore Land Transport Authority is moving toward Q2 launch for vulnerable commuter training in Mandarin. Simon & Sabine's Australian coaching program has a clear automation blocker but is willing to commit if the integration architecture is feasible. Anne Blocker / ESI, a long-time customer on two platforms, gave extensive feedback that perfectly aligns with the Learning Experience team's top 3 priorities (learning paths, quizzes, certificates). Internally, the sales council rallied behind targeting CE credential providers, while the win/loss review surfaced recurring blockers: SCORM, cart/bundle checkout, custom checkout fields, and pricing page confusion continue to cost deals.
